zh: 10. 黑格尔的哲学革命
en: 10. Hegel’s Revolution in Philosophy

zh: 顺便说一句，不难看出，我们所处的时代是一个诞生与向新时期过渡的时代。精神已经与其以往的生活和思想世界决裂，并即将把它淹没在过去之中；它正在进行自身的转变。事实上，精神从未停歇，而是始终在向前发展。但正如婴儿在经历了漫长而平静的滋养后吸入的第一口气，打破了单纯量变增长的渐进性——这是一次质的飞跃——婴儿由此诞生；同样，自我修养的精神也正缓慢而平静地成熟为新的形态，一点一点地瓦解着它先前世界的结构，而该结构的不稳定性仅通过零星的征兆得以显现；侵蚀既定秩序的轻浮与厌倦，以及对未知事物的模糊预感，都是即将到来的变革的先兆。这种并未改变整体面貌的渐进式瓦解，被日出所中断——日出如闪电般，霎时间揭示出新世界的轮廓。
en: Incidentally, it is not difficult to see that our time is a time of birth and of transition to a new period. Spirit has broken with the previous world of its life and ideas, and is on the point of submerging it in the past; it is at work on its own transformation. Indeed, spirit is never at rest but always engaged in moving forward. But just as the first breath drawn by a child after its long, quiet nourishment breaks the gradualness of merely quantitative growth – a qualitative leap – and now the child is born, so the spirit that cultivates itself matures slowly and quietly into its new shape, dissolving bit by bit the structure of its previous world, whose instability is indicated only by isolated symptoms; the frivolity and boredom that infest the established order, the vague foreboding of something unknown, are heralds of approaching change. This gradual crumbling that did not alter the physiognomy of the whole is interrupted by the sunrise which, like lightning, all of a sudden reveals the contour of the new world.

zh: 黑格尔的“探索之旅”
en: HEGEL’S ‘VOYAGE OF DISCOVERY’

zh: 格奥尔格·威廉·弗里德里希·黑格尔于1770 年出生于斯图加特。青年时期，他先是追随谢林，随后成为其合作者；谢林因其激进观点而小有恶名，直到晚年才与普鲁士当局和解。但黑格尔很快便超越了早期的探索。黑格尔对哲学的原创性贡献始于1807 年《精神现象学》的出版。这一时期正值风起云涌、动荡不安的年代。当他还是十九岁的学生时，法国革命已然爆发。法国大革命和拿破仑战争给整个时代留下了不可磨灭的印记。用黑格尔自己的话来说，“该书的撰写是在耶拿战役前夕的午夜完成的。”
en: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was born in Stuttgart in 1770. In his youth he was a follower, and then a collaborator of Schelling, whose radical views gained him a certain notoriety, until he made his peace with the Prussian authorities in later life. But Hegel soon moved on from his early efforts. Hegel’s original contribution to philosophy begins in 1807 with the publication of The Phenomenology of Spirit. The period under consideration was one of storm and stress. France had erupted in revolution when he was a nineteen-year-old student. The French Revolution and the Napoleonic Wars set an indelible stamp on the entire epoch. In Hegel’s own words, the “composition of the book was concluded at mid-night before the battle of Jena.”

zh: 这部被黑格尔称为“探索之旅”的作品，却遭到了他昔日的恩师和朋友们的冷遇与不满。
en: This work, which Hegel describes as his voyage of discovery was received with coldness and dissatisfaction by those who had previously been his teachers and friends.

zh: 《精神现象学》追溯了思想在各个阶段的发展历程，从最低层、最一般和最抽象的形式，逐步发展到最高形式，即黑格尔所称的“概念”。每一种认识形式都在其自身的条件和局限内加以考察，从而揭示出它与其他思想形式之间的辩证关系。在此，黑格尔的方法阐明了哲学的重要性：唯有哲学必须审视并论证其自身的概念，这与数学截然不同——数学是从被不加批判地接受的既定公理出发的。哲学不预设任何东西，甚至不预设它自身。
en: The Phenomenology traces the development of thought through all its phases, proceeding from the lowest, most general and abstract, to the highest form, which he calls the Notion. Each form of knowledge is examined within its own conditions and limits, bringing out its dialectical relation to other forms of thought. Here, Hegel’s method illustrates the importance of philosophy: it alone must consider and justify its own conceptions, unlike mathematics, which proceeds from given axioms which are accepted uncritically. Philosophy presupposes nothing, not even itself.

zh: 对于现代读者而言，黑格尔的著作颇具难度——恩格斯曾称其为“抽象而晦涩”。《精神现象学》无疑正是如此。有时，人们会觉得黑格尔是在刻意故弄玄虚，仿佛在挑战读者去穿透辩证思维那复杂而艰深的体系。事实上，困难的很大一部分源于黑格尔是一位唯心主义者，因此，辩证法在这里呈现为一种神秘化的形式。《精神现象学》就是这一点的典型例证。
en: For the modern reader, the writings of Hegel present considerable difficulties – Abstract and abstruse, Engels called them. This is certainly true of The Phenomenology. At times, one has the impression that Hegel is being deliberately obscure, that he is challenging the reader to penetrate the complex and difficult edifice of dialectical thought. A large part of the difficulty, in fact, stems from the fact that Hegel was an idealist and that, therefore, the dialectic appears here in a mystified form. The Phenomenology is a good example of this.

zh: 在这里，历史发展以一种唯心主义的方式呈现，即作为自我意识（或精神）的发展。尽管如此，我们仍可以像马克思那样，从唯物主义的视角来解读黑格尔，从而揭示其思想中的理性内核。在《精神现象学》中，“自我意识”通过感觉、知觉以及观念等多种方式展现其活动。在这一切之中，我们可以窥见发生在自然、社会和人类精神中的真实过程的模糊轮廓。与先前的唯心主义哲学不同，黑格尔对自然事实、人性及人类历史表现出了浓厚的兴趣。在他抽象的表述背后，蕴藏着关于历史、哲学和当代科学各个方面的丰富知识。马克思称他为当时最具百科全书式博学的人。
en: Here, historical development appears in an idealistic fashion, as the development of self-conscious mind (or spirit). Nevertheless, it is possible to read Hegel, as Marx did, from a materialist point of view, bringing out the rational kernel of his thought. In The Phenomenology, ‘self-consciousness’ reveals its activity in many ways, through sensation and perception, as well as through ideas. In all this, it is possible to perceive the dim outline of real processes that take place in nature, society, and the human mind. In contrast with previous idealist philosophies, Hegel displayed a lively interest in the facts of nature, human nature, and human history. Behind his abstract presentation, there lies a wealth of knowledge of all aspects of history, philosophy and contemporary science. Marx described him as the most encyclopaedic mind of the day.

zh: 一旦剥离了唯心主义的神秘化包装，在“抽象而晦涩”的语言背后，我们便会看到一场人类思想的全面革命。俄罗斯激进民主主义者赫尔岑将黑格尔的辩证法称为“革命的代数”。
在代数方程中，必须填入缺失的量。后来，马克思和恩格斯做到了这一点：他们在黑格尔去世后挽救了其哲学中的理性内核，并将其置于唯物主义基础上，赋予其科学性质。恩格斯在评论黑格尔哲学时写道：
en: Behind the ‘abstract and abstruse’ language, once the idealist mystification is stripped away, we see before us a fully fledged revolution in human thought. The Russian radical democrat Herzen referred to the Hegelian dialectic as “the algebra of revolution.”

In an algebraic equation it is necessary to fill in the missing quantities. This was later achieved by Marx and Engels, who rescued the rational kernel of Hegel’s philosophy after his death, and, by placing it on a materialist basis, gave it a scientific character. Commenting on Hegel’s philosophy, Engels writes:

zh: 这种新的德国哲学在黑格尔体系中达到了顶峰。在这个体系中——这正是它的巨大功绩——整个世界，无论是自然的、历史的还是思想的，首次被呈现为一个过程，即处于不断的运动、变化、转化和发展之中；并且试图追溯使所有这些运动和发展构成一个连续整体的内在联系。从这一角度来看，人类历史不再呈现为毫无意义的暴力行径的狂乱漩涡——在成熟的哲学理性审判席前，这些行径皆应受到同等谴责，最好尽快被遗忘——而是人类自身的进化过程。现在，理性的任务就是追踪这一过程在所有曲折道路上的渐进行进，并揭示贯穿所有看似偶然现象的内在规律。
en: This new German philosophy culminated in the Hegelian system. In this system – and herein is its great merit – for the first time the whole world, natural, historical, intellectual, is represented as a process, i.e., as in constant motion, change, transformation, development; and the attempt is made to trace out the internal connection that makes a continuous whole of all this movement and development. From this point of view the history of mankind no longer appeared as a wild whirl of senseless deeds of violence, all equally condemnable at the judgement-seat of mature philosophic reason and which are best forgotten as quickly as possible, but as the process of evolution of man himself. It was now the task of the intellect to follow the gradual march of this process through all its devious ways, and to trace out the inner law running through all its apparently accidental phenomena.

zh: 今天的黑格尔
en: HEGEL TODAY

zh: 黑格尔是一位远超其时代的天才。遗憾的是，十九世纪初自然科学的水平尚不足以提供充分的信息，使他能够充分发挥其革命性新方法的作用，尽管他曾有过一些卓越的洞见。恩格斯在《自然辩证法》这部辩证写作的杰作中，将这一方法应用于科学领域。但在我们这个时代，科学已经提供了大量材料，证明了黑格尔基本思想的正确性。二十世纪缺乏一位黑格尔来为这些伟大的发现提供必要的洞见，这真是一场悲剧。
en: Hegel was a genius who was far ahead of his time. Unfortunately, the level of the natural sciences at the beginning of the nineteenth century did not furnish enough information to allow him to apply his revolutionary new method to full effect, although he had some brilliant insights. Engels applied this method to science in Dialectics of Nature, a masterpiece of dialectical writing. But in our own time, science has furnished a wealth of material which shows the correctness of Hegel’s fundamental ideas. It is a tragedy that the twentieth century lacked a Hegel to provide the necessary insights into these great discoveries.

zh: 如今，许多科学家对哲学抱有轻蔑的态度，认为哲学对他们的研究是多余的。他们认为，科学所取得的实际进步使他们远远凌驾于哲学之上。然而实际上，他们甚至远不及哲学最原始的水平。常言道，自然厌恶真空。在缺乏一套连贯且成熟的哲学体系的情况下，他们便沦为各种偏见和错误观念的牺牲品——这些观念是他们从所处社会的流行趋势和氛围中无意识地吸收而来的。这些浮渣与残骸，加之大学时期汲取的关于拙劣哲学的零星模糊记忆，构成了许多所谓受过教育的人（包括科学家）全部的智力行囊。正如黑格尔幽默地指出的，这些“完全等同于这次旅程，可以同样好地替代它，正如据说菊苣可以替代咖啡一样”。
en: Nowadays, many scientists adopt a contemptuous attitude towards philosophy, which they regard as superfluous to their requirements. They consider that the actual progress made by science places them far above philosophy. In reality, however, they are far below philosophy at its most primitive level. It is said that nature abhors a vacuum. In the absence of a consistent and worked-out philosophy, they fall prey to all kind of prejudices and false ideas which they unconsciously imbibe from the prevailing tendencies and mood in society in which they live. This flotsam and jetsam, together with a few confused recollections of bad philosophy they picked up at university, provide the sum total of the intellectual baggage of many supposedly educated people, including scientists. As Hegel humorously observed, these are “perfect equivalent of this journey and as good a substitute for it as chicory is reputed to be for coffee”.

zh: 在过去一个半世纪里，黑格尔一直被可悲地忽视。西方哲学的主流学派——后现代主义、分析哲学和逻辑实证主义（后者部分是作为对黑格尔主义的反动而诞生的）——对待黑格尔的态度，恰如极端新教徒对待罗马教皇一般。反过来，这一哲学派别的观点又影响了许多科学家。西方现代科学家中，极少数愿意给予黑格尔应有评价的，当属比利时科学家伊利亚·普里戈金。他提出了混沌与复杂性理论，这一思想脉络与辩证法有着诸多共通之处。否定黑格尔（或恩格斯）其实非常简单，因为他们关于科学的论述必然受到当时科学实际发展水平的限制。然而，令人惊叹的是，黑格尔的科学观点实际上是多么先进。
en: For the last century-and-a-half, Hegel has been sadly neglected. The dominant schools of Western philosophy, Postmodernism, analytic philosophy and logical positivism (the latter of which was born partly as a reaction against Hegelianism), have treated Hegel rather as extreme Protestants treat the Pope of Rome. In turn, the views of this philosophical sect has influenced many scientists. One of the very few modern scientists in the West who has been prepared to give Hegel his due is the Belgian Ilya Prigogine, who has developed the theory of chaos and complexity, a line of thinking which has much in common with dialectics. It is a very simple matter to dismiss Hegel (or Engels) because their writings on science were necessarily limited by the actual state of science of the day. What is remarkable, however, is how advanced Hegel’s views on science actually were.

zh: 普里戈金和斯滕格斯在《混沌中的秩序》一书中指出，在牛顿思想被普遍奉为圭臬的时代，黑格尔就已拒绝了古典牛顿物理学的机械论方法：
en: In their book Order out of Chaos, Prigogine and Stengers point out that Hegel rejected the mechanistic method of classical Newtonian physics, at a time when Newton’s ideas were universally sacrosanct:

zh: 黑格尔的自然哲学系统性地包容了牛顿科学所否定的一切。特别是，它立足于力学所描述的简单行为与生物等更复杂实体的行为之间的质的差异。它否认将这些层次还原的可能性，驳斥了“差异仅是表象”以及“自然在本质上同质且简单”的观念。它肯定了层次结构的存在，每个层次都以之前的层次为前提。
en: The Hegelian philosophy of nature systematically incorporates all that is denied by Newtonian science. In particular, it rests on the qualitative difference between the simple behaviour described by mechanics and the behaviour of more complex entities such as living beings. It denies the possibility of reducing those levels, rejecting the idea that differences are merely apparent and that nature is basically homogeneous and simple. It affirms the existence of a hierarchy, each level of which presupposes the preceding ones.

zh: 普里戈金和斯滕格斯指出，恰恰在黑格尔对牛顿机械论的批判已被证明是正确的时候，他却遭受了不公正的忽视：
en: Prigogine and Stengers refer to the unjust neglect from which Hegel has suffered, precisely at a time when his criticisms of Newtonian mechanism had been shown to be correct:

zh: 从某种意义上说，黑格尔的体系为时间与复杂性这两个关键问题提供了一种自洽的哲学回应。然而，对于几代科学家而言，它却是极度厌恶与蔑视的对象。短短几年内，黑格尔自然哲学固有的困难因其体系所依据的科学背景过时而进一步加剧——毕竟，黑格尔对牛顿体系的否定正是基于他那个时代的科学观念。而正是这些观念，以惊人的速度被遗忘了。很难想象还有比十九世纪初更不合时宜的时期，去为古典科学的替代方案寻求实验和理论支持。尽管这一时期以科学实验范围的显著扩展以及看似与牛顿科学相矛盾的理论层出不穷为特征，但其中大多数理论在问世仅数年后便不得不被放弃。
en: In a sense Hegel’s system provides a consistent philosophic response to the crucial problems of time and complexity. However, for generations of scientists it represented the epitome of abhorrence and contempt. In a few years, the intrinsic difficulties of Hegel’s philosophy of nature were aggravated by the obsolescence of the scientific background on which his system was based, for Hegel, of course, based his rejection of the Newtonian system on the scientific conceptions of his time. And it was precisely those conceptions that were to fall into oblivion with astonishing speed. It is difficult to imagine a less opportune time than the beginning of the nineteenth century for seeking experimental and theoretical support for an alternative to classical science. Although this time was characterised by a remarkable extension of the experimental scope of science and by a proliferation of theories that seemed to contradict Newtonian science, most of those theories had to be given up only a few years after their appearance.

zh: 对此只需补充几点。首先，黑格尔哲学的价值不在于其体系，而在于辩证法。黑格尔著作之所以晦涩难懂，部分原因恰恰在于他试图将自己所发展的、极为精妙的辩证法，强行塞进一个任意的唯心主义哲学体系的枷锁之中。当辩证法无法契合该体系时，他便诉诸各种诡辩手段和奇特的推理方式，这使得整套理论变得极其曲折晦涩。
en: There are only a couple of things that need to be added to this. Firstly, what was valuable in Hegel’s philosophy was not his system, but the dialectical method. Part of the reason why Hegel’s writings are obscure is precisely that he tried to force the dialectic – which he developed brilliantly – into the straitjacket of an arbitrary idealist philosophical system. When it did not fit, he resorted to all manner of subterfuges and peculiar modes of reasoning which make the whole thing extremely convoluted and obscure.

zh: 然而，我们坚信，针对黑格尔的那场可耻阴谋的主要原因，与他文风晦涩毫无关系。这在100 年前并未让大学教授们感到担忧。此外，与逻辑实证主义者那些毫无意义的语言迂回相比，黑格尔文风的晦涩根本不值一提——尽管无人知晓原因，这些逻辑实证主义者却被奉为“连贯思维”的典范。不，黑格尔成为一个被抹去地位的人物的真正原因，在于人们意识到他的辩证法哲学是马克思和恩格斯革命思想的出发点。可怜的老黑格尔，现实生活中是个保守派，却因牵连而在缺席审判中被定罪。
en: However, we are firmly convinced that the main reason for the shameful conspiracy against Hegel has nothing to do with the obscurity of his style. That did not worry the university professors 100 years ago. Moreover, the obscurity of Hegel is nothing compared to the senseless linguistic meanderings of the logical positivists, who are held up as models of ‘coherent thought’, though nobody quite knows why. No, the real reason why Hegel became converted into a non-person is because it was realised that his dialectical philosophy was the point of departure for the revolutionary ideas of Marx and Engels. Poor old Hegel, conservative in real life, has been tried in his absence and found guilty by association.

zh: 对黑格尔思想的恐惧既非偶然，也非错误。即使在十九世纪，有些人已经清楚地认识到辩证法所构成的危险。杰出的英国“黑格尔主义者”詹姆斯·斯特林在1867 年写道：“在我看来，这种辩证法不仅在黑格尔那里，也在其他人那里导致了许多模棱两可之处，未来还可能成为一种祸患。”
甚至在黑格尔生前，其哲学所蕴含的革命意味就已开始令普鲁士当局感到不安。1815 年法国战败后，整个欧洲迎来了一段反动时期。1819年的所谓《卡尔斯巴德法令》将普鲁士管辖范围内所有地区的大学置于宗教裁判所式的控制之下。最微小的异议都被视为颠覆行为。在马克思后来讽刺地称为“卷心菜容克贵族”的普鲁士封建贵族统治的土地上，弥漫着一种令人窒息的狭隘地方主义氛围。
en: The fear of Hegel’s ideas is neither accidental nor mistaken. Even in the nineteenth century, the danger posed by the dialectic was clear to some. James Stirling, a prominent English ‘Hegelian’, wrote in 1867: “This dialectic, it appears to me, has led to much that is equivocal both in Hegel and in others, and may become a pest yet.”

Even during his lifetime, the revolutionary implications of Hegel’s philosophy began to disturb the Prussian authorities. The defeat of the French in 1815 ushered in a period of reaction all over Europe. The so-called Carlsbad decrees of 1819 subjected the universities in all areas under Prussian jurisdiction to inquisitorial control. The slightest non-conformity was looked upon as subversion. A stifling atmosphere of petty provincialism prevailed in the lands of the ‘cabbage Junkers’, as Marx later ironically called the Prussian feudal aristocrats.

zh: 在柏林——黑格尔任教的大学所在地——他的敌人散布恶毒的谣言，称他的思想违背基督教教义，甚至根本就是无神论。从那时起，他就成了众矢之的。面对理性主义者和福音派人士的双重攻击，黑格尔进行了有力的辩护，指出：“关于宗教的所有思辨哲学都可能走向无神论：这完全取决于谁来阐述；我们这个时代特有的虔诚以及煽动者的恶意，将使我们不乏这样的阐述者。”
en: In Berlin, where Hegel taught at the university, spiteful rumours were put in circulation by Hegel’s enemies that his ideas were un-Christian, or even downright atheism. From then on, he was a marked man. Attacked by both Rationalists and Evangelicals, Hegel defended himself vigorously, pointing out that “all speculative philosophy on religion may be carried to atheism: all depends on who carries it; the peculiar piety of our times and the malevolence of demagogues will not let us want carriers.”

zh: 迫害氛围如此浓重，以至于黑格尔甚至考虑过移居比利时——正如马克思后来所做的那样。1827 年，他在给妻子的信中提到，他考察了列日大学和鲁汶大学，觉得这些地方或许有朝一日能成为他的避风港，“当柏林的牧师们让库普费尔格拉本对他来说完全无法忍受时”。“罗马教廷，”他补充道，“比柏林那些可悲的神职人员们所形成的卑劣阴谋集团，是一个更值得尊敬的对手。”
颇具讽刺意味的是，在生命晚期，这位保守且虔诚的黑格尔竟被视为危险的激进分子。然而，反动派们的怀疑背后，确实不无道理。黑格尔的哲学中隐藏着革命思想的萌芽，这种思想将改变世界。这本身就是辩证矛盾最显著的例证！
en: Such was the atmosphere of persecution that Hegel even considered moving to Belgium, as Marx later did. In 1827, he wrote a letter to his wife commenting that he had looked at the universities of Liège and Louvain with the feeling that they might one day provide him a resting place, “when the parsons in Berlin make the Kupfergraben completely intolerable for him”. “The Roman Curia”, he added, “would be a more honourable opponent than the miserable cabals of a miserable boiling of parsons in Berlin”.

It is ironic that at the end of his life, the conservative and religious Hegel should be regarded as a dangerous radical. Yet there was more than a grain of truth behind the suspicions of the reactionaries. Hidden within the philosophy of Hegel was the germ of a revolutionary idea, which would transform the world. This, in itself, constitutes the most remarkable example of a dialectical contradiction!

zh: 在《哲学史》中，黑格尔揭示了不同思想学派之间隐含的辩证关系，阐明了各种理论如何揭示真理的不同方面——这些方面与其说是相互矛盾，不如说是相互补充、相互完善。在《哲学科学百科全书》中，黑格尔同样试图将整个科学呈现为一个有机统一的整体。它不仅仅是一门科学汇编或一部哲学知识词典，而是作为辩证相互关联的总体而呈现的科学。这是一个非常现代的概念。
en: In his History of Philosophy Hegel revealed the hidden dialectical relationship between different schools of thought, showing how different theories revealed different aspects of the truth, which do not so much contradict, as complement and complete one another. In the Encyclopaedia of the Philosophical Sciences, Hegel likewise attempts to show the whole of science as an integrally collective whole. It is not merely a collection of sciences or a dictionary of philosophical knowledge but science presented as a dialectically interrelated totality. This is a very modern conception.

zh: 黑格尔并非意图否定或推翻先前的哲学，而是旨在总结所有先前的思想学派，从而达成一种辩证的综合。但在这一过程中，他将哲学推到了极限。超越这一界限，若不将其转变为另一种形态，便无法继续发展哲学。可以说，自黑格尔以来，关于主要哲学问题，实际上已无新论。此后那些自诩新颖独创的哲学流派，只不过是在翻炒旧观念，而且无一例外地以更肤浅、更令人不满意的方式进行。自黑格尔以来，哲学领域唯一的真正革命是由马克思和恩格斯发起的，它突破了哲学作为单纯智力活动的局限，将其带入了实践的领域以及改变社会的斗争之中。
en: Hegel did not set out to deny or demolish previous philosophy, but to summarise all previous schools of thought, and arrive at a dialectical synthesis. But in so doing, he pushed philosophy to its limits. Beyond this point, it was impossible to develop philosophy without transforming it into something different. It is possible to say that, since Hegel, nothing new has really been said on the main philosophical questions. Subsequent schools of philosophy, which purport to be new and original, merely rehash old ideas, invariably in a more superficial and unsatisfactory manner. The only real revolution in philosophy since Hegel was the one effected by Marx and Engels, which passes beyond the limits of philosophy as a merely intellectual exercise, and carries it into the realm of practice and the struggle to change society.

zh: 黑格尔在《哲学史》中指出：“精神的存在就是它的活动，而它的活动就是对自身的认识。”但在黑格尔那里，思考不仅仅是一种沉思活动。思维的最高形式——理性——并非仅仅接受既定事实，而是对事实进行加工并加以转化。在黑格尔那里，思维与存在之间、“主体”与“客体”之间的矛盾，是通过认识过程本身得以克服的，这一过程不断深入地渗透到客观世界之中。然而，从唯物主义的角度来看，思维并非一种孤立的活动，而是与人类的整体存在密不可分。人类是通过具体的、感性的活动来发展思维的，而不仅仅是通过智力活动。通过劳动改造物质世界，人们同时也改造着自己，并在此过程中发展和拓展了思维的视野。这种辩证观念的要素在黑格尔那里已经初见端倪。马克思所做的，就是剥去其唯心主义的外衣，并以清晰而科学的方式加以阐述。
en: Hegel says in the History of Philosophy that “the being of mind is its act, and its act is to be aware of itself.” But in Hegel, thinking is not merely a contemplative activity. The highest form of thought, reason, does not merely accept the given facts, but works upon them and transforms them. The contradiction between thought and being, between ‘subject’ and ‘object’, is overcome in Hegel through the process of knowledge itself, which penetrates ever deeper into the objective world. From a materialist point of view, however, thinking is not an isolated activity, but is inseparable from human existence in general. Mankind develops thought through concrete, sensuous activity, not merely intellectual activity. By transforming the material world through labour, men and women also transform themselves, and, in so doing, develop and extend the horizon of their thinking. In embryo, the elements of this dialectical conception are already present in Hegel. What Marx did was to strip it of its idealist disguise, and express it in a clear and scientific manner.

zh: 认识论
en: THEORY OF KNOWLEDGE

zh: 正如我们所见，哲学的基本问题之一是思想与存在之间的关系。意识（知识）与客观世界之间是什么关系？康德主张，思考的主体与不可知的“物自体”之间存在着无法逾越的鸿沟。黑格尔则以不同的方式提出这一问题。思维过程就是主体与客体的统一。思维并非将人与客观世界隔开的屏障，相反，它是将二者联系起来（“中介”）的过程。以感官知觉中直接给定的现实为出发点，人类思维并非像洛克所设想的那样被动地接受，而是开始运作，对这些信息进行转化，将其分解为各个组成部分，然后重新组合起来。人运用理性思维超越直接现实。辩证思维在分析给定现象时，将其分解为各个组成部分，并揭示赋予该现象以生命和运动的那些矛盾特征与趋势。
en: As we have seen, one of the fundamental problems of philosophy is the relation between thought and being. What is the relation between consciousness (knowledge) and the objective world? Kant claimed that there was an unbridgeable gap between the thinking subject and the unknowable Thing-in-Itself. Hegel poses the question differently. The process of thinking is the unity of subject and object. Thought is not a barrier separating man from the objective world, but, on the contrary, is a process linking (‘mediating’) the two. Taking as its starting point the reality immediately given in sense-perception, human thought does not merely passively accept, as Locke imagined, but sets to work, transforming this information, breaking it down into its component parts, and putting it together again. Man uses rational thought to go beyond immediate reality. Dialectical thought, in analysing a given phenomenon, divides it into its component parts and demonstrates those contradictory features and tendencies which give it life and movement.

zh: 科学知识并非仅仅由具体事物的目录构成。如果我们说“所有动物”，这还算不上动物学。在事实之上，必须发现规律和客观过程。必须揭示事物之间的客观关系，并解释一种状态向另一种状态的过渡。科学史，如同哲学史一样，是一个永恒的肯定与否定的过程，是一个无休止的进程与发展，其中一种思想否定另一种思想，而自身又被否定，形成了一个在深化我们对自身和宇宙认识的永无止境的过程。在婴儿的智力发展中也可以看到类似的现象。
en: Scientific knowledge does not consist of a mere catalogue of particular items. If we say ‘all animals’, that is not yet zoology. Above and beyond the facts, it is necessary to discover laws and objective processes. It is necessary to uncover the objective relations between things, and explain the transitions between one state and the other. The history of science, like that of philosophy, is a permanent process of affirmation and negation, a ceaseless process and development, in which one idea negates another, and, in its turn, is negated in a never-ending process of deepening our knowledge of ourselves and the universe. A similar phenomenon may be seen in the mental development of the infant.

zh: 黑格尔的伟大功绩在于揭示了人类思想发展的辩证性质：从胚胎阶段开始，经历一系列阶段，最终抵达理性的最高阶段——概念。用黑格尔的术语来说，这就是从“自在”到“自在自为”的过程，也就是说，从未发展、隐含的存在到发展、显性的存在。人类胚胎在潜能上是一个人，但它还不是“自在自为”的人。为了实现其全部潜能，需要经历一个完整的发展时期，其中婴幼儿期、青春期和中年期构成了必要的阶段。儿童的思想显然具有不成熟的特征。但即便是青年表达出的正确观点，其分量也远不及由一位饱经人生沧桑、因而对这些话语的实际含义有着更深刻理解的老人所表达的相同观点。
en: Hegel’s great merit was to show the dialectical character of the development of human thought, from its embryonic phase, passing through a whole series of stages, and finally arriving at the highest stage of reason: the Notion. In Hegelian language, it is the process from being ‘in itself’ to being ‘in and for itself’, that is to say, from undeveloped, implicit being to developed and explicit being. The human embryo is, potentially, a human being, but it is not a human being in and for itself. In order to realise its full potential, a whole period of development is necessary, in which infancy, adolescence and middle age constitute necessary stages. The thought of a child evidently has an immature character. But even a correct idea expressed by a youth does not have the same weight as the same idea expressed by an old person, who has experienced life, and consequently has a deeper understanding of what these words actually mean.

zh: 在黑格尔那里，人类的实际发展被以一种神秘的形式呈现出来，即作为精神的发展。作为一位唯心主义者，黑格尔对社会的发展并没有真正的认识，尽管他的著作中对历史唯物主义有一些精彩的预见。思想在这里被呈现为“绝对理念”的表达，这是一个神秘的概念，正如恩格斯讽刺地指出的那样，我们唯一了解的，就是他对此绝对什么也没告诉我们。实际上，思想是人类大脑和神经系统的产物，与人体密不可分；而人体又依赖于食物，食物的获取则以人类社会和生产关系为前提。
en: In Hegel, the real development of human beings is presented in a mystical form, as the development of spirit. As an idealist, Hegel had no real conception of the development of society, although there are some brilliant anticipations of historical materialism in his writings. Thought appears here as an expression of the Absolute Idea, a mystical concept about which the only thing we learn, as Engels ironically put it, is that he tells us absolutely nothing about it. In reality, thought is the product of the human brain and nervous system, inseparable from the human body, which, in turn, depends upon food, which, in turn, presupposes human society and productive relations.

zh: 思想是“会思考的物质”的产物，是自然的最高成就。无生命物质具有产生生命的潜能。即便是最低等的生命形式也具备感觉性和兴奋性，这些特质在高等动物身上，具有形成神经系统和大脑的潜能。黑格尔的“自我意识”不过是一种奇幻的方式，来表达真实的人类如何逐步意识到自身及其所处世界的历史过程。这一过程既非易事，也非自动发生，正如个体人在从婴儿期过渡到成年期时，意识也不会自动形成。在这两种情况下，该过程都是通过一系列漫长且往往充满创伤的阶段来实现的。人类思想的发展——正如哲学、科学以及整个文化史所反映的那样——展现为一个充满矛盾的过程：一个阶段取代另一个阶段，而它自身随后又会被新的阶段所取代。这不是一条直线，而是一条不断中断的轨迹，其中夹杂着停滞、踉跄甚至倒退的时期，但这些时期不过是为新的进步铺平了道路。
en: Thought is a product of matter that thinks, the highest achievement of nature. Inanimate matter possesses the potential to produce life. Even the lowest forms of life possess sensibility, irritability, which has the potential to produce, in higher animals, a nervous system and a brain. Hegel’s ‘self-consciousness’ is merely a fantastic way of expressing the historical process by which real human beings gradually become conscious of themselves and the world in which they live. This does not come about easily or automatically, any more than the individual human being automatically acquires consciousness in the transition from infancy to adulthood. In both cases, the process takes place through a prolonged and often traumatic series of stages. The development of human thought, as reflected in the history of philosophy and science, and of culture in general, reveals itself as a contradictory process, in which one stage supersedes another, and, in its turn, is superseded. It is not a straight line, but one that is continuously interrupted, with periods of stagnation, faltering and even reversals, which, however, merely prepare the ground for new advances.

zh: 思想是如何发展的
en: HOW THOUGHT DEVELOPS

zh: 人类思维的最初起源，即处于直接而原始阶段的思维，就是感官知觉：原始人类通过感官，首先记录并记忆环境直接提供的信息，却尚未理解这些信息背后的真实本质、因果关系和规律。基于观察和经验，人类思维逐渐开始进行一些或多或少具有抽象性质的概括。这一过程经历了一段长达数百万年的漫长而艰辛的历程，起初极其缓慢，但在最近一万年中却迅速积聚了势头。然而，尽管思想和科学取得了巨大的进步，普通人的思维仍停留在相当原始的水平上。
en: The very beginnings of human thought, mind in its immediate and primitive stage, is sense perception: primitive humans, through his senses, begins by registering and memorising the data immediately provided by his environment, without understanding the true nature, causal relationships and laws which underlie them. From observation and experience, gradually the human mind proceeds to make a number of generalisations of a more or less abstract character. This process involves a long and laborious journey lasting several millions of years, extremely slow at first, but rapidly gathering momentum in the last ten thousand years. Yet, despite the colossal strides made by thought and science, ordinary thinking remains on quite a primitive level.

zh: 当我们初次思考任何课题时，首先形成的是对整体的观念，而未能把握所有具体内容和细微的相互联系。这仅仅是一个大致的轮廓和赤裸裸的抽象概念。因此，爱奥尼亚学派的哲学家们，甚至佛教，都直觉地将宇宙把握为一个不断变化的辩证整体。但这种初步概念缺乏任何定义和具体性。有必要更进一步，为这一总体图景提供明确的表述，分析并阐明其内容之间的精确关系。它必须经过分析和量化。没有这一点，科学便无从谈起。这就是粗糙、直接、未发展的思维与科学本身之间的区别。
en: When we first consider any subject, we first form a notion of the whole, without grasping all the concrete content and detailed interconnections. It is merely a general outline and a bare abstraction. Thus, the Ionic philosophers and even Buddhism intuitively grasped the universe as a constantly changing dialectical whole. But this initial notion lacks all definition and concreteness. It is necessary to go further and provide the general picture with a definite expression, analysing and specifying the precise relations of its content. It has to be analysed and quantified. Without this, science in general is impossible. This is the difference between crude, immediate, undeveloped thought and science as such.

zh: 在人类意识的曙光中，男女并未将自身与自然明确区分开来，正如新生婴儿无法将自己与母亲区分开来一样。在漫长的岁月中，人类逐渐学会了区分，学会了通过在周围令人困惑的自然现象网络中发现焦点来认识世界，学会了观察、比较、概括并得出结论。就这样，在无数个千年里，一系列重要的概括从经验中逐渐形成，并最终凝结成我们所熟悉的思维模式——正因为我们对它们如此熟悉，才往往视其为理所当然。
en: At the dawn of human consciousness, men and women did not clearly distinguish themselves from nature, just as a newborn baby does not distinguish itself from its mother. Gradually, over a long period, humans learned to distinguish, to cognize the world, by detecting focal points in the bewildering web of natural phenomena surrounding them, to observe, compare, generalise, and draw conclusions. In this way, over countless millennia, a series of important generalisations were built up from experience, which gradually came to crystallise into the familiar forms of thought which, because we are so familiar with them, we take for granted.

zh: 常见的日常思维在很大程度上依赖于感官知觉、直接经验、表象，以及那种被称为“常识”的、由经验与肤浅思考混合而成的独特产物。这些通常足以让我们度过一生。但它们不足以达到科学的理解，而且在某个阶段，它们会失效，甚至在实际应用中也变得毫无用处。我们必须超越感官知觉的直接经验，去把握常具欺骗性的表象背后的普遍过程、规律和隐蔽联系。
en: Common, everyday thought relies heavily on sense perception, immediate experience, appearances, and that peculiar hybrid of experience and superficial thinking called ‘common sense’. These things are normally sufficient to carry us through life. But they are insufficient to arrive at a scientific understanding and, at a certain point, break down and become useless even for practical purposes. It is necessary to go beyond the immediate experience of sense perception, and to grasp the general processes, laws and hidden relations which lie beyond frequently deceptive appearance.

zh: 普通人的思维倾向于固守具体而熟悉的事物。接受那些看似固定且众所周知的观念，要比接受那些挑战熟悉与惯例的新思想容易得多。惯例、传统、习俗和社会规范在社会中代表着一股强大的力量，类似于力学中的惯性力。在正常时期，大多数人都不愿质疑他们所生活的社会：其道德、意识形态和财产形式。各种偏见、政治观念、“科学”正统论都被不加批判地接受，直到人们生活中发生某些深刻变化，迫使他们对现状提出质疑。
en: Ordinary human thought prefers to cling to what is concrete and familiar. It is easier to accept what is apparently fixed and well known rather than new ideas which challenge what is familiar and customary. Routine, tradition, custom and social convention represent a powerful force in society, akin to the force of inertia in mechanics. In normal periods, most people are reluctant to question the society in which they live: its morality, ideology and property forms. All kinds of prejudices, political ideas, ‘scientific’ orthodoxy are accepted uncritically, until some profound change in people’s lives forces them to question what is.

zh: 社会和思想上的从众心理是最常见的自我欺骗形式。人们仅仅因为熟悉，就认为熟悉的思想是正确的。因此，尽管与真理毫无关系，但私有制、金钱和资产阶级家庭是生活永恒且不变的特征这一观念，却已深深植根于大众意识之中。辩证法与这种肤浅而平庸的思维方式截然相反。正因为它挑战了熟悉的观念，所以常常会引起激烈的反对。怎么可能挑战同一律呢？这一法则陈述了看似显而易见的事实，即“A”等于“A”。这一所谓的法则是某种普遍偏见的逻辑反映，即认为万物就是其本身，绝非其他；认为万物一成不变。相反，辩证法则从截然相反的观点出发，认为万物都在变化，都在产生和消亡。
en: Social and intellectual conformism is the commonest form of self-deception. Familiar ideas are taken to be correct just because they are familiar. Thus, the notion that private property, money and the bourgeois family are eternal and unchanging features of life has sunk deeply into the popular consciousness, although it bears no relation whatsoever to the truth. Dialectics is the direct opposite of this superficial and commonplace way of thinking. Precisely because it challenges familiar ideas, it frequently arouses fierce opposition. How is it possible to challenge the law of identity, which states what seems obvious, that ‘A’ equals ‘A’? This so-called law is the logical reflection of a popular prejudice, that everything is what it is, and nothing else; that nothing changes. Dialectics, on the contrary, sets out from the opposite point of view, that everything changes, comes into being and passes away.

zh: 经验主义思想家声称要“如实”看待事物，自以为非常务实和具体。但实际上，事物并不总是表象那样，往往会变成其对立面。这种直接的感性认识是最低级的认识，就像婴儿的认知一样。对现实的真正科学理解，要求我们对感官知觉提供的信息进行分解，从而揭示所考察事物的真实本质。更深入的分析总会揭示出，即使是最看似固定、坚实且不可改变的事物，其背后也存在着矛盾的趋势，这些趋势最终将导致它们转变为其对立面。正是这些矛盾，构成了整个自然界中一切生命、运动和发展的源泉。为了获得真正的理解，我们必须不仅将事物视为“它们现在的样子”，还要将其视为“它们曾经的样子”，以及“它们必然会成为的样子”。
en: The empiricist thinker, who claims to take things ‘as they are’, imagines himself to be very practical and concrete. But, in reality, things are not always what they seem to be, and frequently turn out to be their opposite. This kind of immediate sensuous knowledge is the lowest kind of knowledge, like that of a baby. A really scientific understanding of reality requires us to break down the information provided by sense perception in order to get at the true nature of the things under consideration. A deeper analysis always reveals the contradictory tendencies which underlie even the most apparently fixed, solid, and immutable things, which eventually will lead to them being transformed into their opposites. It is precisely these contradictions which are the source of all life, movement and development throughout nature. In order to get a real understanding, it is necessary to take things, not just as they are, but also as they have been, and as they necessarily will become.

zh: 对于简单的日常事务，形式逻辑和“常识”就足够了。但一旦超越了某些界限，它们就不再适用。此时，辩证法就变得绝对必要。与无法把握矛盾并试图消除矛盾的形式逻辑不同，辩证法代表着矛盾的逻辑，而矛盾是自然和思维的一个基本方面。通过分析过程，辩证法揭示了这些矛盾，并展示了它们是如何得到解决的。然而，新的矛盾总是不断出现，从而催生出一个永无止境的发展螺旋。这一过程在科学和哲学的整个发展历程中都可见一斑，它们正是通过矛盾而发展的。这绝非偶然。它反映了人类知识作为无限过程的本质：一个问题的解决会立即引发新的问题，而这些问题又会被解决，如此循环往复，无穷无尽。
en: For simple everyday purposes, formal logic and ‘common sense’ are sufficient. But beyond certain limits it no longer applies. At this point dialectics becomes absolutely essential. Unlike formal logic, which cannot grasp contradictions and seeks to eliminate them, dialectics represents the logic of contradiction, which is a fundamental aspect of nature and thought. By a process of analysis, dialectics reveals these contradictions and shows how they are resolved. However, new contradictions always appear, thus giving rise to a never-ending spiral of development. This process can be seen in the entire development of science and philosophy, which takes place through contradictions. This is not an accident. It reflects the nature of human knowledge as an infinite process in which the solution of one problem immediately gives rise to new ones, which are in turn resolved, and so on ad infinitum.

zh: 如果我们从感官经验层面上最基础的知识形式出发，形式逻辑和“常识”的局限性很快就会显露出来。思维只是将我们所发现的事实如实记录下来。乍看之下，感官知觉的真理似乎简单而不言自明。人们可以自信地依赖它们，但经仔细考察，事情并非如此简单。那些看似坚实可靠的事物，结果却并非如此。我们脚下的立足点开始动摇。
en: If we set out from the most elementary form of knowledge at the level of sense-experience, the limitations of formal logic and ‘common sense’ very soon become clear. The mind simply registers the facts as we find them. At first sight, the truths of sense perception seem to be simple and self-evident. They can be confidently relied upon, but on closer examination, things are not so simple. What appears to be solid and reliable turns out not to be so. The ground begins to shift beneath our feet.

zh: 感性确信始于“此处”与“当下”。对此，黑格尔指出：
en: Sense-certainty sets out from the ‘here’ and the ‘now’. Of this Hegel says:

zh: 因此，我们必须向感性确信本身提出这个问题：什么是“此”？如果我们将“此”以其存在的双重形态——即“现在”和“此处”——来理解，那么它所蕴含的辩证法将获得一种与“此”本身同样可理解的形式。对于“什么是现在？”这个问题，我们例如可以回答：“现在是夜晚。”为了检验这种感性确信的真实性，一个简单的实验就足够了。我们将这一真理记录下来；真理因被记录下来而不会失去任何东西，也不会因我们保存它而失去任何东西。如果现在，就在今天中午，我们再次审视这段写下的真理，我们就不得不说它已经变得陈旧了。
en: So we have to put the question to sensory certainty itself: What is the This? If we take the This in the twofold shape of its Being, as the Now and as the Here, the dialectic it has in it will receive a form as intelligible as the This itself is. To the question: What is the Now? we answer, for example: The Now is the night. In order to test the truth of this sensory certainty a simple experiment suffices. We write down this truth; a truth cannot lose anything by being written down, nor can it lose anything through our preserving it. If now, this noon, we look again at the written truth we shall have to say that it has become stale.

zh: 黑格尔的这一评论让人联想到芝诺关于运动的著名悖论。例如，如果我们想要确定一支飞箭的位置，说出它此刻所在之处，就在我们指向它的那一瞬间，它已经飞过去了，因此“此刻”并非某种“存在”，而是某种“曾经存在”过的事物。如此一来，起初看似为真的，最终却被证明是假的。原因在于运动本身的矛盾性质。运动是一个过程，而不是孤立点的集合。同样，时间是由无限多个“现在”汇聚而成的。同样地，“此处”原来并非单一的“此处”，而是包含前方与后方、上方与下方、右侧与左侧。此刻作为一棵树存在于此的事物，下一分钟便会作为一栋房子，或是其他什么东西，依然存在于此。
en: This comment of Hegel recalls the famous paradoxes of Zeno in relation to motion. For example, if we wish to fix the position of an arrow flying, to say where it is now, the moment that we point to it, it has already passed, and therefore the ‘now’ is not something that is, but something that has been. Thus, what initially appears to be true, turns out to be false. The reason is to be found in the contradictory nature of movement itself. Movement is a process, not a collection of separate points. Similarly, time consists of an infinite number of ‘nows’, all taken together. Likewise, the ‘here’ turns out to be not a single ‘here’, but a before and a behind, and an above and a below, and a right and a left. What is here, as a tree, the next minute is here as a house, or something else.

zh: 辩证思维与形式思维
en: DIALECTICAL AND FORMAL THINKING

zh: 正确运用辩证法，意味着研究者必须完全沉浸于对研究对象的探究之中，从各个方面对其进行考察，以确定其存在的内在矛盾及其运动的必然规律。这种方法的经典范例可见于马克思的《资本论》三卷本。马克思并非任意地发明了支配资本主义生产方式的规律，而是通过对资本主义各个方面的细致入微的辩证分析，追溯其历史发展，并追踪商品生产过程的各个阶段，从而得出了这些规律。
en: The correct application of the dialectical method means that the investigator must completely immerse himself in the study of the object, examining it from all sides in order to determine the inner contradictions and necessary laws of motion which govern its existence. The classical example of this method is to be found in the three volumes of Marx’s Capital. Marx did not invent the laws which govern the capitalist mode of production in an arbitrary fashion, but derived them from a painstaking dialectical analysis of all aspects of capitalism, tracing its historical development and following the process of commodity production through all its phases.

zh: 列宁在其《哲学笔记》中——该著作对黑格尔的《逻辑学》进行了详细研究——指出，辩证思维的首要条件是：“从概念自身出发对概念进行规定（必须在事物本身的关系和发展中考察事物本身）。”
或者换一种说法，辩证法以“考察的客观性（不是例子，不是差异，而是物自体）”为出发点。
en: In his Philosophical Notebooks, which contain a detailed study of Hegel’s Science of Logic, Lenin points out that the first condition for dialectical thought is: “The determination of the concept out of itself (the thing itself must be considered in its relations and in its development).”
Or, put another way, the dialectical method sets out from “the objectivity of consideration (not examples, not divergences, but the Thing-in-itself).”

zh: 思维的第一种也是最低级的形式是感性知觉，即我们的感官直接向我们提供的信息——我们所看到、听到、触摸到的等等。紧随其后的是知性（Verstand），它试图解释“是什么”，但这种解释是片面的，仅记录孤立的事实。广义而言，此处的知性与形式逻辑、日常思维以及“常识”是相同的。我们看到某物存在，它就是它本身，且除了它本身之外别无他物。似乎无需多言。但实际上，还有许多话要说。知性将事物呈现为孤立、固定且一成不变的。然而，现实却完全不是这样。
en: The first and lowest form of thought is sense-perception, that is to say, the information immediately given to us by our senses – what we see, hear, touch, etc. This is followed by understanding (Verstand), which attempts to explain what is, but does so in a one-sided way, registering isolated facts. Broadly speaking, the understanding here is identical with formal logic, ordinary thinking, and ‘common sense’. We see that a thing exists, that it is itself, and nothing but itself. There seems nothing more to be said. But, in reality, there is a great deal more to be said. The understanding presents things as isolated, fixed and unchanging. Reality, however, is not like that at all.

zh: 一种更高级的思维形式，正是黑格尔（以及康德）所称的“理性”（Vernunft）。理性试图超越知性所确立的直接事实，将其分解、消解，并在看似坚实的外部表象背后，揭示内在的矛盾趋势——这些趋势迟早会导致深刻的转变。黑格尔说：“理性的斗争，就是为了打破知性将一切所归结的僵化状态。”
en: A more advanced form of thinking is what Hegel (and Kant) call Reason (Vernunft). Reason attempts to go beyond the immediate facts established by understanding, to break them down, dissolve them, and behind the apparently solid exterior appearances, to reveal the inner contradictory tendencies, which, sooner or later, will lead to profound transformations. “The battle of reason”, says Hegel, “is the struggle to break up the rigidity to which the understanding has reduced everything.”

zh: 辩证思维的第一原则是绝对客观性。必须客观地对待研究对象，且不得预先设想最终结果。我们必须全身心投入研究对象，直到不仅掌握一系列孤立的事实，而且把握它们的内在联系和规律性。辩证法的规律，与形式逻辑不同，并非可以从外部任意套用到任何具体内容上的任意构造。它们源于对自然、社会和人类思想发展的仔细观察。
en: The first principle of dialectical thought is absolute objectivity. The subject matter must be approached objectively, and the final result must not be anticipated in advance. We must absorb ourselves in the subject matter, until we grasp not just a series of isolated facts, but their inner connection and lawfulness. The laws of dialectics, unlike formal logic, are not arbitrary constructions which can be applied in an external manner to any particular content. They have been derived from a careful observation of the development of nature, society and human thought.

zh: 以形式逻辑为代表的常规思维形式，可以以一种外部的、任意的方式应用于任何研究对象。事实上，研究对象的实际内容与之完全无关。形式逻辑，正如抽象的同一律（“A”等于“A”）所表达的那样，似乎表述了一个无可争议的真理。实际上，这不过是一个空洞的同义反复，一种“单色形式主义”，或者正如黑格尔机智地所言：“那黑夜里……所有的牛都是黑的——这就是认知的空洞天真。”
en: The usual forms of thought represented by formal logic can be applied to any subject matter in an external and arbitrary fashion. Indeed, the real content of the subject matter is entirely irrelevant to it. Formal logic, as expressed in the abstract law of identity (‘A’ equals ‘A’) appears to express an indisputable truth. In reality, it is an empty tautology, “monochrome formalism”, or as Hegel says wittily, “the night in which … all cows are black – this is the naiveté of emptiness of cognition.”

zh: 所谓的同一律仅仅是一种没有实际内容的抽象形式，既无法运动也无法进一步发展。它无法应用于一个永不停息的宇宙的动态现实之中——在这个宇宙中，万物不断变化、产生并消亡，因此不能被视为自相等同。同样，矛盾律也是错误的，因为每一个真实存在的事物都同时包含肯定与否定。它既是又非，正因为它处于持续的运动与变化之中。唯一不变的，就是变化本身。所有试图将真理固定为一种片面且静止的事物的尝试注定要失败。矛盾的存在在大众意识中以谚语和俗语的形式得到了直观的反映，然而，由于其缺乏系统性而具有直觉性的特点，这些谚语和俗语往往相互矛盾。例如，“甲之肉，乙之毒。”
en: The so-called law of identity is only an abstract form with no real content, incapable of movement or further development. It cannot be applied to the dynamic reality of a restless universe, in which everything constantly changes, comes into being, and passes away, and therefore cannot be considered self-equal. In the same way, the law of contradiction is false because every really existing thing contains both positive and negative. It is and it is not because it is in a constant state of movement and change. The only thing which does not change is change itself. All attempts to fix the truth as a one-sided and static thing are doomed to failure. The existence of contradiction is reflected intuitively in the popular consciousness in the form of proverbs and sayings which, however, because of their unsystematic and intuitive character, often contradict each other. For example, “One man’s meat is another man’s poison.”

zh: 在科学中，我们同样可以在各个层面看到矛盾，例如吸引和排斥、磁性的南北极、电的正负、力学中的作用与反作用、收缩与膨胀等。与形式逻辑不同，辩证法并非强加于自然，而是从现实本身中推导出其范畴。真正的辩证法与其批评者所描绘的讽刺性形象毫无共同之处——这些批评者试图将其描绘成一种主观而任意的文字游戏。这实际上是诡辩法的辩证法，它与形式逻辑一样，也是以一种外部的方式应用于任何既定内容，意图以主观的方式操纵矛盾。辩证法也与康德所采纳并将其变成死板的公式的“三段式”（正题、反题、合题）这种粗糙的简化毫无共同之处。真正的辩证法试图通过严谨客观的分析，发现特定现象的内在逻辑和运动规律。
en: In science also we see contradictions at all levels, for example attraction and repulsion, north and south in magnetism, positive and negative in electricity, action and reaction in mechanics, contraction and expansion, etc. As against formal logic, dialectics does not inflict itself on nature, but derives its categories from reality itself. Real dialectics has nothing in common with the caricature outlined by its critics, who try to present it as a subjective and arbitrary play on words. This is really the dialectic of Sophism, which, like formal logic, is also applied in an external manner to any given content with the intention of manipulating contradictions in a subjective manner. Nor does dialectics have anything in common with the gross oversimplification of the ‘triad’ (thesis, antithesis, synthesis), which was adopted by Kant and turned into a lifeless formula. Real dialectics attempts to discover, by means of a rigorously objective analysis, the inner logic and laws of motion of a given phenomenon.

zh: 黑格尔的《逻辑学》
en: HEGEL’S ‘LOGIC’

zh: 黑格尔的《逻辑学》是人类思想的巅峰之作之一。它系统地阐述并发展了所有思维形式，从较为原始、未成熟的思维，直至黑格尔所称的“概念”这一最高形式的辩证推理。
en: The Logic of Hegel is one of the pinnacles of human thought. It is the systematic exposition and development of all the forms of thought, from the more primitive undeveloped thought, up to the highest form of dialectical reasoning, which Hegel calls the Notion.

zh: 他从尽可能普遍的命题——“纯粹存在”——出发，这一命题似乎无需进一步证明。从这一极其抽象的概念出发，他循序渐进，沿着从抽象到具体的进程不断推进。
en: He sets out with the most general proposition possible – that of ‘pure being’ – something that seems to require no further proof. From this extremely abstract idea, he proceeds, step by step, along a process which leads from the abstract to the concrete.

zh: 这一推理过程分阶段进行，每个阶段都否定前一阶段。思想史，尤其是哲学和科学史，表明知识正是通过这种方式获得的——在一个永无止境的过程中，我们对宇宙运行规律的认识日益精确。在黑格尔的理论中，每个阶段刚被肯定便随即被否定，其结果是形成一个更高、更丰富、更具体的概念。
en: This process of reasoning proceeds by stages, in which each stage negates the previous one. The history of thought, particularly that of philosophy and science, shows that knowledge is acquired precisely in this way, in a never-ending process whereby we obtain an increasingly precise idea of the workings of the universe. In Hegel, each stage is no sooner affirmed than it is negated, and the result is a higher, richer, more concrete idea.

zh: 从总体框架来看，黑格尔的《逻辑学》可分为三个主要部分：《存在论》、《本质论》和《概念论》。黑格尔从思维中最根本的范畴——“存在”这一范畴——开始阐述他的哲学。显然，我们所考虑的任何事物，在其他一切之前都必须存在。这似乎是我们一切知识的基础。但事情并非如此简单。如果仅仅陈述“存在”这一事实，而不提供进一步的细节，我们便无法深入理解。我们渴望了解更多。但一旦我们从“一般存在”这一抽象概念转向更具体的概念，存在便会转化为它的对立面。黑格尔指出，一般意义上的存在等同于——无。
en: In general outline, Hegel’s Logic can be divided into three main parts: The Doctrine of Being, The Doctrine of Essence (essential nature) and the Doctrine of the Notion. Hegel begins his philosophy with the most fundamental category of thought – the category of Being. Evidently, anything which we consider must exist, before anything else. This seems to be the basis of all our knowledge. But things are not so simple as that. The bare statement of existence, without further details, does not get us very far. We want to know more. But the moment we pass from the abstract idea of being in general to a more concrete idea, being turns into its opposite. Hegel shows that being in general is the same as – nothing.

zh: 这一观点看似奇怪，但实际上在许多不同层面上都能被证明是正确的。如果我们试图从事物中消除一切矛盾，并固守“事物仅仅是存在”这一观念，最终将得出截然相反的结论，因为没有“非存在”就不可能有“存在”，正如没有死亡就不可能有生命，没有黑暗就不可能有光明。长期在北极生活的人都知道，对人的视觉而言，无尽的白色与绝对的黑色所产生的效果是相同的。
en: This idea seems strange, but actually can be seen to be true on many different levels. If we try to eliminate all contradiction from things, and cling to the idea that they just are, we arrive at the opposite conclusion, because there can be no being without not-being, just as there can be no life without death, and no light without darkness. People who have spent a long time in the Arctic know that the effect of unrelieved whiteness is the same as that of total blackness to the human vision.

zh: 事实上，这是一种空洞的抽象，因为它缺乏一切具体性。在现实中，存在与无的辩证统一就是“生成”，即变化的过程。这就是赫拉克利特所说的“万物既存在又不存在”的含义，因为万物都在流变之中。每个人都从经验中知道，事物往往并非表面所见到的那样。那些看似稳定、以至于我们可以断言“它们是”的事物，经仔细考察后却发现其实并不稳定，最终会转变为其他事物，从而“不是”。此外，这种“有”与“无”之间的矛盾正是所有生命与运动的基础。
en: It is, in fact, an empty abstraction, since it lacks all concreteness. In reality, the dialectical unity of being and nothing is becoming, that is the process of change. This is what Heraclitus meant when he said everything is and is not, because everything is in flux. Everyone knows from experience that things are frequently not what they seem to be. Things that appear to be stable, so that we can say ‘they are’, on closer examination turn out to be unstable, and change into something else, and they ‘are not’. Moreover, this contradiction between being and not being is the basis of all life and movement.

zh: 在黑格尔的理论中，“存在”这一范畴代表着原始、未发展的思维阶段。它仅被视为一种潜能，如同幼儿或早期原始人类的思维。这是一种胚胎期的思维。胚胎最初仅是一个单独的细胞，没有明确发育的特征。它尚无法被明确识别为人类。为了发育，它必须首先否定自身。在细胞内部，存在着相互矛盾的倾向，这些倾向引发了内部分化的过程。当这些相互冲突的倾向达到一定程度时，细胞便分裂为两个。最初那个未分化的细胞已不复存在。它已被消除、被否定。然而与此同时，它也被保留下来，并提升到了更高的层次。这一过程反复进行多次，从而产生日益完善的组织结构和更高的复杂性，特征也愈发清晰可辨，最终孕育出一个完全成熟的人。
en: In Hegel, the category of being represents the stage of primitive, undeveloped thought. It is thought only as a potential, like the thought of a small child, or early proto-humans. It is embryonic thought. An embryo begins as a single cell, with no clearly developed features. It is not clearly identifiable as a human being. In order to develop, it must first negate itself. Inside the cell, there are contradictory tendencies which give rise to a process of inner differentiation. When these conflicting tendencies reach a certain point, the cell divides in two. The original, undifferentiated cell has ceased to exist. It has been cancelled, negated. Yet at the same time, it has been preserved, and carried onto a higher level. The process is repeated many times, giving rise to increasing organisation and greater complexity, with more clearly distinguishable features, eventually giving rise to a fully-fledged human being.

zh: 关键在于，在现实生活中，事物的否定方面与肯定方面同样重要。我们习惯于将生与死视为截然相反的两极。但在实际上，它们是同一个过程的两个部分，密不可分。生命、生长和发展的过程，只能通过有机体所有细胞的不断更新来实现——有些细胞死亡，有些细胞诞生。即使在最原始的层面上，生命也涉及持续的变化：有机体不断从环境中吸收养分并利用它们来构建自身，同时排出废物。因此，每一个生命体既存在又不存在，因为万物都处于持续变动的状态。没有矛盾就意味着缺乏一切内在的差异，没有运动，处于静态平衡的状态——简而言之，就是死亡。
en: The point is that, in real life, the negative side of things is equally as important as the positive. We are accustomed to look upon life and death as completely opposite poles. But in practice, they are two parts of the same process, and are inseparable. The process of life, growth and development can only take place through the constant renewal of all the cells of the organism, some dying, others coming into being. Even on the most primitive level, life involves constant change in which the organism constantly absorbs food from its surroundings and uses it to build itself, while getting rid of waste matter. Therefore, every living thing is and is not at the same time, because everything is in a constant state of flux. To be without contradiction is to lack all inner differentiation, to have no movement, to be in a state of static equilibrium – in a word, to be dead.

zh: 用普里戈金和斯滕格斯的话来说：
en: In the words of Prigogine and Stengers:

zh: 活细胞展现出永不停息的新陈代谢活动。其中同时发生着成千上万种化学反应，以转化细胞摄取的物质、合成基础生物分子并排出代谢废物。无论是反应速率的差异还是细胞内的反应位点，这种化学活动都高度协调。因此，生物结构兼具秩序与活性。相比之下，平衡状态即使具有结构，也依然处于惰性状态，例如晶体便是如此。
en: The living cell presents an incessant metabolic activity. There thousands of chemical reactions take place simultaneously to transform the matter the cell feeds on, to synthesise the fundamental biomolecules, and to eliminate waste products. As regards both the different reaction rates and the reaction sites within the cell, this chemical activity is highly coordinated. The biological structure thus combines order and activity. In contrast, an equilibrium state remains inert even though it may be structured, as, for example, with a crystal.

zh: 乍看之下，这些观察似乎只是无谓的琐碎之谈。事实上，它们是极其深刻的思考，不仅适用于思维，也适用于自然。而且，尽管并不总是显而易见，但无生命的大自然也是如此。事实上，黑格尔认为二者是密不可分的。“万物皆流，无物常驻”，赫拉克利特如是说。“我们既踏入又不踏入同一条河流。”
黑格尔在此表达的正是同样的观点。这种哲学的核心是一种动态的宇宙观；这种观点将事物视为有生命的进程，而非死物；着眼于它们本质的相互关系，而非孤立的碎片或任意的罗列；将其视为一个整体，它大于各部分之和。
en: At first sight, these observations may seem like pointless subtleties. In point of fact, they are extremely profound reflections, which are not only applicable to thought, but also to nature. And, although it is not always obvious, the same is true of inanimate nature also. Indeed, Hegel considered that the two were inseparably linked. “Everything flows and nothing stays”, said Heraclitus. “We step and we do not step into the same stream”.

Hegel here is saying the same thing. At the heart of this philosophy is a dynamic view of the universe; a view which deals with things as living processes, not dead objects; in their essential interrelations, not separate bits and pieces, or arbitrary lists; as a whole, which is greater than the sum of the parts.

zh: 量与质
en: QUANTITY AND QUALITY

zh: 万物都可以从两个角度来看待——质和量。世界由不断变化的过程总和构成这一事实，并不意味着现实事物没有明确的存在形式，即同一性。无论一个对象发生多大变化，在一定限度内，它仍然是一种在质上与其他事物有别、且与之不同的存在形式。正是这种质的规定性赋予事物以稳定性，使它们相互区别，并使世界如此丰富且变化无穷。
en: Everything can be seen from two points of view – quality and quantity. The fact that the world consists of a sum total of processes which are constantly changing does not mean that real things do not have a definite form of existence, an identity. However much an object changes, it remains, within certain limits, a qualitatively distinct form of existence, different from another. It is this qualitative definiteness which gives things stability, differentiates them, and makes the world so rich and boundlessly varied.

zh: 事物的属性使它成为它自身。但这种质不能还原为其各个单独的属性，而是与事物作为整体紧密相连。因此，人不仅仅是由骨骼组织、血液、肌肉等组成的集合体。生命本身是一种复杂的现象，不能简单归结为其各个分子的总和，而是源于它们之间的相互作用。用现代复杂性理论的术语来说，生命是一种涌现现象。
en: The properties of a thing are what makes it what it is. But this quality is not reducible to its separate properties. It is bound up with the object as a whole. Thus, a human being is not just an assemblage of bone tissue, blood, muscles, etc. Life itself is a complex phenomenon which cannot be reduced to the sum total of its individual molecules, but arises from the interactions between them. To use the modern terminology of complexity theory, life is an emergent phenomenon.

zh: 黑格尔曾对整体与部分的关系进行了详尽论述，他写道：
en: The relation of whole and parts was dealt with at length by Hegel, who wrote:

zh: 例如，有机体的四肢和器官并非仅仅是其组成部分：只有在统一性中，它们才是它们本身，而且它们无疑受到这种统一性的影响，同时也反过来影响着它。这些四肢和器官只有在解剖学家的手中，才成为单纯的组成部分，而须知，其研究对象并非活体，而是尸体。并非说这种分析不合理：我们只是要说明，若要从真实层面研究有机生命，仅凭整体与部分之间的外部机械关系是远远不够的。
en: The limbs and organs, for instance, of an organic body are not merely parts of it: it is only in their unity that they are what they are, and they are unquestionably affected by that unity, as they also in turn affect it. These limbs and organs become mere parts, only when they pass under the hands of the anatomist, whose occupation, be it remembered, is not with the living body but with the corpse. Not that such analysis is illegitimate: we only mean that the external and mechanical relation of whole and parts is not sufficient for us, if we want to study organic life in its truth.

zh: 值得注意的是，那些最近引起科学界重要群体关注的新思想——混沌理论和复杂性理论——早在很久以前就被黑格尔预见了，而且在许多方面，黑格尔对此进行了更为全面的论述。一个典型的例子是他对“量变引起质变”的解释，即微小变化的积累会引发质的突变。
en: It is interesting to note that the latest ideas which have caught the imagination of an important section of the scientific community – the theories of chaos and complexity – were anticipated long ago by Hegel and, in many respects, received a much more comprehensive treatment in his hands. A case in point is his explanation of the transformation of quantity into quality, whereby an accumulation of small changes brings about a sudden change in quality.

zh: 除了界定事物本质特征的“质”之外，万物还具有“量”的特征——即确定的大小、数量、体积、过程的速度、性质的发展程度等等。事物的量的一面，使其能够（实际或思想上）被分解为构成部分，并重新组合起来。与质不同，量的变化不会改变整体的性质，也不会导致其毁灭。只有当达到一个确定的限度——这个限度在每种情况下都不尽相同——量上的变化才会引发突如其来的质的飞跃。
en: In addition to the quality which defines the essential features of an object, all things possess quantitative features – a definite magnitude, number, volume, speed of its processes, degree of development of its properties, and so on. The quantitative side of things is that which permits them to be divided (actually or mentally) into their constituent parts and put together again. In contrast to quality, changes in quantity do not alter the nature of the whole, or cause its destruction. Only when a definite limit is reached, which is different in each case, do changes of quantitative character cause a sudden qualitative transformation.

zh: 在数学中，事物的定量方面与其内容相分离，并被视为独立的存在。数学之所以能广泛应用于内容截然不同的自然科学和技术领域，正是因为它纯粹处理定量关系。据此，人们声称可以将质还原为量。这就是马克思和恩格斯所指的“形而上学的思维方式”，而如今则被称为还原论。现实世界中没有任何事物仅由量构成，正如没有任何事物是纯粹的质一样。现实中的万物都由量与质的统一体构成，黑格尔称之为“度”。
en: In mathematics, the quantitative aspect of things is separated from their content and regarded as something independent. The extremely wide field of applicability of mathematics to spheres of natural science and technology with very different contents is explained by the fact that it deals purely with quantitative relations. Here, it is claimed, it is possible to reduce quality to quantity. This is the fundamental error of which Marx and Engels referred to as the metaphysical mode of thought, and which nowadays is termed reductionism. There is nothing in the real world that consists only of quantity, just as there is nothing which is pure quality. Everything in reality consists of the unity of quantity and quality, which Hegel called Measure.

zh: “度”即量与质的有机统一。正如我们所见，每一个在质上截然不同的对象，都包含着可变且动态的量的要素。生物体以一定的速率生长；气体和液体受温度变化的影响；一滴水或一堆沙子的行为由其大小决定，诸如此类。然而，这些变化必然受到明确界限的约束，这些界限在每种情况下各不相同，但在实践中通常可以被发现。一旦超越这一界限，量变就会引发质变。而质变反过来又会导致其量属性的变化。不仅存在量变到质变的过程，还存在相反的过程，即质变导致量变。从一种状态向另一种状态过渡的临界点，在黑格尔的“度的节点线”中被表述为节点。
en: Measure is the organic unity of quantity and quality. Every qualitatively distinct object, as we have seen, contains quantitative elements which are mobile and variable. Living organisms grow at a certain rate. Gases and liquids are affected by variations in temperature. The behaviour of a water droplet or a heap of sand is determined by its size, and so on. These mutations, however, are necessarily bounded by definite limits, which are different in each case, but in practice can usually be discovered. Carried beyond this limit, quantitative changes bring about a qualitative transformation. In its turn, the qualitative change brings about a change in its quantitative attributes. There are not only changes of quantity to quality, but also the opposite process, where a change in quality causes a change in quantity. The critical points of transition from one state to another are expressed as nodal points in Hegel’s nodal line of measurement.

zh: 本质
en: ESSENCE

zh: “本质论”是黑格尔哲学中最重要的一部分，因为正是在这里，他详细阐释了辩证法。人的思想并不止步于感官知觉中直接呈现的内容，而是试图超越它，把握“物自体”。在现象之外，我们寻求事物的本质。但这并非立即可及的。我们可以看见太阳和月亮，却无法“看见”万有引力定律。为了超越现象，必须积极调动思维，分解我们先前通过知性所认识的内容。如果知性是肯定的，即断言某事物“是”，那么辩证推理本质上是否定的，因为它瓦解了“是”，并揭示出必然会摧毁它的内在矛盾。
en: The Doctrine of Essence is the most important part of Hegel’s philosophy, because it is here that he explains the dialectic in detail. Human thought does not stop at what is immediately given in sense perception, but seeks to go beyond it and grasp the thing-in-itself. Beyond appearance, we look for the essence of a thing. But this is not immediately accessible. We can see the sun and moon, but we cannot ‘see’ the laws of gravity. In order to go beyond appearance, the mind must be actively brought into play, to break down what we earlier learned through understanding. If the understanding is positive, asserting that a given thing ‘is’, dialectical reasoning is essentially negative, in that it dissolves what ‘is’, and reveals the inner contradictions, which will inevitably destroy it.

zh: 存在于万物核心的矛盾，被表述为“对立统一”这一理念。从辩证角度看，那些看似相互排斥的现象实际上是不可分割的，正如黑格尔所解释的：
en: The contradiction which lies at the heart of all things is expressed as the idea of the unity of opposites. Dialectically, what seem to be mutually exclusive phenomena are actually inseparable, as Hegel explains:

zh: “肯定”与“否定”本应表达一种绝对的差异。然而，二者从根本上说是一样的：其中一方的名称可以转用于另一方。例如，债务和资产并不是两种具体的、自存的财产种类。对债务人而言是“否定”的，对债权人而言就是“肯定”的。通往东方的道路也是通往西方的道路。因此，“肯定”与“否定”在本质上相互制约，并且仅在相互关系中才存在。磁铁的北极不能没有南极，反之亦然。如果我们将一块磁铁切成两半，其中一块不会只有北极，另一块只有南极。同样，在电学中，正电荷和负电荷也不是两种不同且独立的流体。
en: Positive and negative are supposed to express an absolute difference. The two however are at bottom the same: the name of either might be transferred to the other. Thus, for example, debts and assets are not two particular, self-subsisting species of property. What is negative to the debtor is positive to the creditor. A way to the east is also a way to the west. Positive and negative are therefore intrinsically conditioned by one another, and are only in relation to each other. The north pole of the magnet cannot be without the south pole, and vice versa. If we cut a magnet in two, we have not a north pole in one piece, and a south pole in the other. Similarly, in electricity, the positive and the negative are not two diverse and independent fluids.

zh: 在分析过程中，黑格尔列举了一系列重要阶段：肯定与否定；必然与偶然；量与质；形式与内容；吸引与排斥；等等。“本质”的一个核心特征在于它的相对性——万物都与其他事物相关联，构成一个普遍的相互作用网络。初级知识（知性）的基本法则是同一律（“A”=“A”）。这通常被视为我们一切认知的基础。在某种程度上，这是正确的。如果没有同一律，连贯的思考将无法实现。我们确认存在的基本事实，并将注意力集中于某一特定事物。然而，同一性预设了差异。猫之所以是猫，正是因为它不是狗、老鼠、大象等等。为了确立同一性，我们必须将某物与另一物进行比较。
en: In the process of analysis, Hegel enumerates a series of important stages: positive and negative; necessity and accident; quantity and quality; form and content; action and repulsion; and so on. One of the central features of Essence is that it is relative – everything is related to something else, in a universal web of interaction. The basic law of elementary knowledge (understanding) is the law of identity (‘A’ = ‘A’). This is generally considered as the basis of all that we know. Up to a point, this is correct. Without the law of identity, coherent thought would be impossible. We ascertain the basic fact of existence, and focus our attention on a particular thing. However, identity presupposes difference. A cat is a cat, because it is not a dog, a mouse, an elephant, and so on. In order to establish identity, we must compare something to another.
body.review: 原文列举中写作 action and repulsion；结合上下文的成对范畴，action 疑为 attraction 之误，中文作“吸引与排斥”，英文保留底本。

zh: 在现实生活中，尽管同一律看似具有绝对性，却没有任何事物像它所暗示的那样纯粹是其自身。万物都由其他一切事物所决定。从这个意义上说，万物都是相对的。正如恩格斯所指出的：
en: In real life, nothing is purely itself, as implied by the law of identity, despite its apparently absolute character. Everything is determined by everything else. In that sense everything is relative. As Engels remarks:

zh: “本质”的各种规定性的真正性质，黑格尔本人曾这样表述（《百科全书》，第一部，第111 节，附释）：“就本质而言，一切都是相对的”（例如，肯定与否定，它们只有在相互关系中才有意义，而并非各自本身）。
en: The true nature of the determinations of ‘essence’ is expressed by Hegel himself (Enzyklopädie, I, paragraph 111, addendum): “In essence everything is relative” (e.g., positive and negative, which have meaning only in their relation, not each for itself).

zh: 不仅如此。没有任何事物像同一律所暗示的那样简单。正如我们在讨论简单细胞或胚胎时所见，具体存在——与单纯“同一性”的纯粹抽象存在相对——必须包含内在的差异性。此外，这种分化蕴含着矛盾的种子。为了发展，为了生存，细胞必须包含向自我瓦解、向分裂、向否定的倾向。这种内在张力，事实上是所有生命的基础。但它也存在于非生命物体中，例如水滴中的表面张力现象——它使分子保持某种秩序——以及无数其他例子。
en: Not only that. Nothing is simple, as also implied in the law of identity. As we saw in relation to the simple cell or embryo, concrete being, as opposed to the purely abstract being of mere ‘identity’, must contain inner differentiation. Moreover, this differentiation contains the seeds of contradiction. In order to develop, in order to live, the cell must contain the tendency toward self-dissolution, towards division, towards negation. This inner tension is, in fact, the basis of all life. But it is also found in non-living objects, such as the phenomenon of surface tension in a drop of water, which holds the molecules in a certain order, and innumerable other examples.

zh: 几个世纪以来，试图将矛盾从思想中驱除一直是逻辑学家们的一种执念。黑格尔是第一个指出，事实上，矛盾是所有真实存在事物的核心的人。如果我们试图像传统形式逻辑那样去构想一个没有矛盾的世界，我们所能达到的无非是将无法解决的矛盾引入思想之中。这就是康德“二律背反”的真正含义。将同一性与差异性割裂开来，试图否认矛盾的存在，都会将思想引向贫瘠而空洞的形式主义。
en: The attempt to banish contradiction from thought has been an obsession of logicians for centuries. Hegel was the first one to show that, in fact, contradiction lies at the heart of everything that really exists. If we attempt to think of the world without contradiction, as traditional formal logic tries to do, all that we achieve is to introduce insoluble contradictions into thought. This was the real meaning of Kant’s ‘antinomies’. To separate identity and difference, to attempt to deny the existence of contradiction, leads thought into a barren and empty formalism.

zh: 现象与本质
en: APPEARANCE AND ESSENCE

zh: 大多数人都意识到“现象具有欺骗性”。然而，这仅在相对意义上成立。为了理解事物的本质，我们必须首先彻底熟悉正是这些“现象”，即我们所能观察到的所有物理特征、属性和倾向。在这样的分析过程中，我们会清楚地看到某些事实可以作为“非本质”而被省略，并逐渐抵达所考察对象的最根本特征。
en: Most people realise that ‘appearances are deceptive’. However, this is only relatively true. In order to arrive at an understanding of the essence of a thing, we must begin by a thorough acquaintance with precisely these ‘appearances’, that is, with all the physical features, properties and tendencies we can observe. In the course of such an analysis, it will become clear that certain facts can be omitted as ‘unessential’ and, gradually, we will arrive at the most fundamental characteristics of the object under consideration.

zh: 人们常对某人说：“是啊，但他其实并非那样。”这暗示着人并非表面所见到的那样。表象是一回事，而本质则被认为截然不同。然而，这种说法并不完全正确。如果我们对某人只是略有了解，那么确实无法仅凭其行为来对他或她形成准确的印象。这种行为可能完全不符合其典型特征。但如果我们与某人相识已久，就有充分的理由相信我们了解其真实面目。我们之所以依据“表象”，恰恰是因为别无他法。圣经上说：“凭着他们的果子，你们就认出他们来”，
这话是正确的。一个人如何生活、如何行事，他就是怎样的人。除此之外，别无他求。
en: It is very common to say about somebody: “Yes, but he’s not really like that.” The implication is that people are not what they seem to be. Appearance is one thing, but essence is supposed to be completely different. However, this is not quite true. If we only have a slight acquaintance with a person, then it is true that we cannot form an accurate impression of him or her on the basis of their conduct. It may be completely untypical. But if we have known people for a long time, we have sufficient reason to believe that we know them as they are. We precisely base ourselves on ‘appearances’ because there is nothing else to base ourselves on. The Bible says “by their fruits shall you know them”,
and that is correct. As a man or woman lives and acts, so they are. There is nothing else to look for.

zh: 这正是康德的根本谬误——他试图在表象与某种超出经验的神秘“事物”之间划清界限——该“事物”被认为永远超出了人类的认知范围。事实上，一旦我们掌握了事物的所有属性，就等同于认识了事物本身。虽然在特定时刻，我们可能因信息匮乏而受到限制，但原则上，没有任何事物永远无法被人类认识，唯有一件事例外——那就是全面了解无限的宇宙。这并非真正的局限，而仅仅是个人有限性与不断揭示新奥秘的无限宇宙之间辩证关系的体现。尽管个人的具体知识是有限的，但一代又一代，全人类的知识与理解的总和却在不断增长。学习的过程永无止境。这恰恰是其魅力与美之所在。
en: This was the fundamental error of Kant, when he tried to draw a line between appearances and some mysterious ‘thing’ that lay beyond experience which was supposed to be forever beyond human knowledge. In fact, once we know all the properties of a thing, we know the thing itself. We may be limited at any given moment in time by lack of information, but, in principle, there is nothing which is forever barred to human knowledge, except one thing – to know everything about an infinite universe. This is no real limitation, but simply an expression of the dialectical relation between the finite nature of individuals, and an infinite universe, which is constantly revealing new secrets. And although the particular knowledge of one person is finite, from one generation to another, the sum-total of knowledge and understanding of humanity increases. The process of learning is never-ending. Precisely in this lies its fascination and its beauty.

zh: 我们从已知出发，去探索未知。一事引出另一事。医生凭借其医学知识和过往经验，仔细考察所有可观察到的症状，从而得出诊断结论。水手则会研究风向和潮汐，以推测出海的可能性。以此方式，本质通过现象得以显现，尽管要从现象过渡到本质，需要一定的技巧和理解力。
en: We set out from what is known, in order to discover what is not known. One thing leads to another. A doctor, basing himself on all his knowledge of medical science and past experience, carefully examines all the available symptoms and arrives at a diagnosis. A sailor will study the wind and tides in order to guess the possibilities of putting to sea. In this way, essence is manifested through appearance, although it requires a certain skill and understanding to pass from the one to the other.

zh: 在处理社会中发生的各种过程时，可能犯下的最大错误之一，就是将其视为静态且固定的——也就是说，从形式逻辑的角度去看待它们。人们经常会遇到这种情况——以“实践智慧”为幌子的狭隘偏见。人们常说“人永远不会改变”、“世事永远如此”以及“太阳底下无新事”。这种肤浅的思维假装深刻，但实际上只是暴露了那种自满的无知。对于此类断言，并未给出任何合理的依据。偶尔会有人试图为其提供生物学依据，含糊地提及所谓“人性”，而我们立刻就能推断出，提出这种观点的人对人类及其本性一无所知。
en: One of the greatest errors it is possible to commit when dealing with the processes that occur in society is to approach them as static and fixed – that is to say, from the standpoint of formal logic. One frequently comes across this kind of thing – narrow-minded prejudice masquerading as ‘practical wisdom’. It is said that ‘people will never change’, ‘things will always be as they are’, and ‘there is nothing new under the sun’. This kind of superficial thought pretends to be profound, but really only reveals the kind of ignorance which is content with itself. No rational reason is given for such assertions. Occasionally an attempt is made to give it a biological basis, with vague references to something called ‘human nature’, from which we instantly deduce that the individual in question knows nothing whatsoever about humans or their nature.

zh: 这种心态严格地局限于其自身对表象世界最肤浅层面的狭隘体验。这很像一个人一直在冰面上滑行，却懒得去探查冰层的厚度。这样的人十次里可能有九次都能安然无恙。然而有一天，他发现自己正在溺于冰冷的水中。就在那一瞬间，他开始意识到，也许那层冰并没有看起来那么坚固。
en: This kind of mentality is strictly limited to its own narrow experience of the world of appearance in the most superficial sense. It is very much like a man who is constantly skating on the surface, without bothering to inquire about the thickness of the ice. Such a person may get away with it nine times out of ten. One day, however, he finds himself drowning in icy water. At that precise moment, he begins to realise that maybe the ice was not as solid as it looked.

zh: “A”就是“A”。你是你。我是我。人就是人。一美元就是一美元。社会就是社会。工会就是工会。这类句子看似令人安心，但实际上毫无实质内容。如果它们真能表达什么的话，那也只是“万物皆如其本然，一切永恒不变”这一观念。然而，经验告诉我们事实并非如此。万物时刻都在变化，而在某个临界点上，微小的量变便可能引发巨大的质变。
en: ‘A’ is ‘A’. You are you. I am myself. People are people. A dollar is a dollar. Society is society. The trade unions are the trade unions. Such sentences seem reassuring, but in fact are empty of all content. Insofar as they express anything at all, it is the idea that everything is itself, and nothing changes. However, experience tells us something different. Things are constantly changing and, at a critical point, small quantitative changes can produce massive transformations.

zh: 形式与内容
en: FORM AND CONTENT

zh: 事物中存在着许多矛盾。例如，形式与内容之间的矛盾。每个园丁都知道，一粒精心种在花盆里的种子会长成一株植物。起初，花盆保护着幼苗，帮助它茁壮成长。但在某个阶段，根系会变得过大，超出了花盆所能容纳的空间。园丁必须将它移出花盆，否则它就会死亡。同样，人类胚胎在母亲的子宫里受到九个月的保护。到了这个时刻，便会到达一个关键阶段：要么将婴儿从母亲体内分离出来，要么双方都将丧生。这些都是形式与内容之间矛盾的例子，人们很容易理解。另一个例子是，地壳下方积聚的力量最终会引发地震。
en: There are many contradictions in things. For instance, the contradiction between form and content. Every gardener knows that a seed carefully planted in a pot will produce a plant. Initially, the pot protects the young plant and helps it to thrive. But at a certain stage, the roots become too big for the space allowed. The gardener must remove it from the pot, or it will die. Similarly, the human embryo is protected by the mother’s womb for nine months. At this point, a critical stage is reached in which, either the baby is separated from the mother’s body, or both will perish. These are examples of the contradiction between form and content which are readily understood. Another example would be the way in which the forces which accumulate beneath the earth’s crust eventually produce an earthquake.

zh: 社会内部也会积聚类似的力量，社会同样存在其“断层线”。这些力量的作用与引发地震的力量一样，是肉眼无法察觉的。对肤浅的观察者而言，一切看似平静。一切看似“正常”。然而，有经验的观察者能够察觉社会中地下活动的征兆，正如称职的地质学家能够解读地震仪一样。托洛茨基曾将理论定义为“预见胜于惊愕”。肤浅和经验主义的思维注定会不断陷入惊愕，就像那个掉进冰窟窿里的人一样。这是将现象与本质、形式与内容混为一谈所付出的代价。
en: Similar forces build up within society, which also has its ‘fault-lines’. The action of these forces is no more visible than those that cause an earthquake. To the superficial observer, nothing is happening. Everything is ‘normal’. The skilled observer, however, is able to detect the symptoms of subterranean activity in society, just as a competent geologist can read a seismograph. Trotsky once defined theory as the superiority of foresight over astonishment. It is the fate of superficial and empirical thought to be constantly astonished, like the man who fell through the ice. It is the price one pays for confusing appearance with essence and form with content.

zh: 事物的本质是其最根本属性的总和。辩证分析的任务就是确定这些属性。在每一种情况下，都会发现现状与那些趋向于瓦解现状的趋势之间存在着潜在的矛盾。在经典力学中，“完美平衡”的概念起着核心作用。事物往往趋向于回归平衡。至少在理论上是如此。在现实生活中，完美的平衡却极为罕见。每当达到平衡时，它往往只是暂时的、不稳定的。发展和变化正是以此为前提的。在医院的重症监护室里，当心电监护仪达到“平衡”状态——即显示一条直线时，这标志着机体的死亡。
en: The essence of a thing is the sum total of its most fundamental properties. The task of dialectical analysis is to determine these. In each case it will be found that there is a potential contradiction between the present state and tendencies which are tending to dissolve it. In classical mechanics, the idea of a perfect equilibrium plays a central role. Things tend to return to equilibrium. That is, at least, in theory. In real life, a perfect equilibrium is a rarity. Whenever equilibrium is reached, it tends to be temporary and unstable. Development and change presuppose this. In the intensive ward of a hospital, when a heart monitor reaches a state of ‘equilibrium’, i.e., a straight line, this signifies death of the organism.

zh: 在谈论事物的属性时，通常使用动词“拥有”：火具有燃烧的属性；人具有呼吸、思考、进食等属性。这种表述会产生误导。一个孩子“拥有”一支冰淇淋；一位女士“拥有”一只狗。此处的关系是偶然的、外在的，因为无论孩子还是女士，即使没有这些东西，依然是孩子和女士。事物并不“拥有”属性——它本身就是其属性的总和。一旦剥离这些属性，我们就一无所有，这正是康德所说的“物自体”的真实含义。这是一个极其重要的观念，科学家们直到现在才开始理解它。整体不能还原为其各部分之和，因为当各部分进入动态关系时，它们自身会发生转变，并产生一种完全新的状况，受质上不同的规律所支配。
en: When referring to the properties of a thing, it is customary to use the verb ‘to have’: fire has the property of burning; a human being has the properties of breathing, thinking, eating, etc. This gives the wrong idea. A child has an ice-cream. A woman has a dog. The relationship here is accidental and external, since the child and the woman could equally well not have these things, and still be a child and a woman. A thing does not ‘have’ properties – it is the sum-total of its properties. Take these away, and we are left with nothing, which is what Kant’s Thing-in-Itself really was. This is an extremely important idea, which is only now beginning to be understood by scientists. The whole cannot be reduced to the sum of its parts, because in entering into a dynamic relationship, the parts themselves become transformed, and give rise to an entirely new situation, governed by qualitatively different laws.

zh: 这种现象在社会中随处可见。托洛茨基指出，没有组织的工人阶级，只不过是“剥削的原料”。

在像当下这样的时期，许多工作场所的工会被取缔或遭到削弱，这一事实显得尤为突出。从历史上看，工人组织起来的运动会彻底改变这种局面。量转变为质。个别工人虽然无力，但作为阶级组织起来的工人阶级却拥有巨大的力量，至少在潜在意义上如此。没有工人阶级的“慷慨允许”，没有一个齿轮会转动，没有一部电话会响，没有一盏灯泡会发光。用黑格尔的术语来说，尚未组织起来的工人阶级仅仅是一个“自在”的阶级——也就是说，是一种未实现的潜能。一旦它组织起来并意识到自己的力量，它就成为“自为”的阶级。当然，黑格尔远未从他的辩证法中得出如此明确的革命性结论。作为一位唯心主义者，他主要关注的是将辩证法呈现为“精神”的发展过程。现实关系被颠倒过来，现实世界被呈现为一种神秘化的形式。但真实的内容却总能穿透唯心主义的浓雾，如同阳光穿透云层一般。
en: This phenomenon can be seen in society. Trotsky pointed out that the working class, without organisation, is only “raw material for exploitation.”

This fact is starkly revealed in periods like the present, when trade unions are eliminated or undermined in many workplaces. Historically, the movement of the workers to organise themselves brings about a complete transformation of the situation. Quantity becomes transformed into quality. Whereas individual workers are powerless, the class organised as a class has colossal power, at least potentially. Not a wheel turns, not a telephone rings, not a light bulb shines without the kind permission of the working class. In Hegelian language, the working class before it is organised, is only a class ‘in itself’ – that is, an unrealised potential. Once it becomes organised and conscious of its power, it becomes a class ‘for itself’. Of course, Hegel was far from drawing such explicitly revolutionary conclusions from his dialectical method. Being an idealist, his main concern was to present the dialectic as the process of development of the Spirit. Real relations are stood on their head, and the real world is presented in a mystified form. But the real content constantly finds its way through the dense fog of idealism, like shafts of sunlight through the clouds.

zh: 本质上，万物都是相对的；也就是说，万物都与一个“他者”处于关系之中，这个“他者”既决定着它，又反过来受其决定。事物之所以是它们本身，正是因为它们与其他事物的相互关系。这一点在社会中同样可见。那些通常被认为是真实实体的事物，实际上是特定关系的产物，这些关系已经深深植根于人们的意识之中，以至于具有了偏见的力量。君主制就是这样一个例子：
en: In essence, everything is relative; that is to say, everything stands in relation to an Other, which conditions it, and in turn, is conditioned by it. Things are what they are thanks to their interrelations with other things. This also can be seen in society. Things which are commonly believed to be real entities are, in fact, the product of particular relationships, which have sunk so deeply into people’s consciousness that they acquire the force of prejudice. Such a thing is the institution of monarchy:

zh: 天真的人认为，王权就存在于国王本人身上，存在于他的貂皮斗篷和王冠之中，存在于他的血肉之躯之中。事实上，王权不过是人际关系的一种体现。国王之所以成为国王，仅仅是因为数百万人的利益与偏见通过他的个人形象折射出来。当发展的洪流冲刷掉这些相互关系时，国王便显得只是一个面容憔悴、下唇松弛的凡人。那个曾被称为阿方索十三世的人，可以凭新近的切身感受来谈论这一点。

由人民意志推举的领袖与由上帝意志指定的领袖之区别在于：前者不得不为自己开辟道路，或者至少要协助事件的交汇来发现自己。尽管如此，领袖始终是人与人之间的关系，是个体对集体需求的回应。关于希特勒人格的争议，越是试图从他自身寻找成功的秘诀，就越显得尖锐。与此同时，很难再找到另一位政治人物，能像他一样成为匿名历史力量的焦点。并非每个愤懑的小资产阶级都能成为希特勒，但每个愤懑的小资产阶级身上，都蕴藏着希特勒的一粒微尘。
en: Naive minds think that the office of kingship lodges in the king himself, in his ermine cloak and his crown, in his flesh and bones. As a matter of fact, the office of kingship is an interrelation between people. The king is king only because the interests and prejudices of millions of people are refracted through his person. When the flood of development sweeps away these interrelations, then the king appears to be only a washed-out man with a flabby lower lip. He who was once called Alfonso XIII could discourse upon this from fresh impressions.

The leader by will of the people differs from the leader by will of God in that the former is compelled to clear the road for himself or, at any rate, to assist the conjuncture of events in discovering him. Nevertheless, the leader is always a relation between people, the individual supply to meet the collective demand. The controversy over Hitler’s personality becomes the sharper the more the secret of his success is sought in himself. In the meantime, another political figure would be difficult to find that is in the same measure the focus of anonymous historic forces. Not every exasperated petty bourgeois could have become Hitler, but a particle of Hitler is lodged in every exasperated petty bourgeois.

zh: 必然性与偶然性
en: NECESSITY AND ACCIDENT

zh: 在进一步分析存在及其各种表现形式的本质时，黑格尔探讨了潜在与现实之间的关系，以及必然性与偶然性（“偶然性”）之间的关系。关于这个问题，有必要澄清黑格尔最著名（或最臭名昭著）的一句话：“凡是合乎理性的都是现实的；凡是现实的都是合乎理性的。”
乍看之下，这一论断似乎令人费解，甚至带有反动色彩，因为它似乎暗示一切存在的事物都是理性的，因此都是正当的。然而，正如恩格斯所解释的那样，这绝非黑格尔的本意：
en: In further analysing the nature of being in all its different manifestations, Hegel deals with the relation between potential and actual, and also between necessity and accident (‘contingency’). In relation to this question, it is important to clarify one of Hegel’s most famous (or notorious) sayings: “What is rational is actual; and what is actual is rational.”

At first sight, this statement seems mystifying, and also reactionary, since it seems to imply that all that exists is rational, and therefore justified. This, however, was not at all what Hegel meant, as Engels explains:

zh: 然而，根据黑格尔的观点，现实性绝非在任何情况下、任何时候都能赋予任何既定社会或政治状况的属性。恰恰相反。罗马共和国是现实的，但取而代之的罗马帝国同样是现实的。1789 年，法国君主制已变得如此不现实——也就是说，它已完全丧失了必然性，变得如此不合理，以至于必须被“大革命”所摧毁；黑格尔始终以极大的热情谈论这场革命。因此，在此情况下，君主制是不现实的，而革命才是现实的。于是，在发展过程中，一切先前现实的事物都变得不现实，丧失了其必然性、其存在的权利及其合理性。而取而代之的，是一种崭新且充满活力的现实——如果旧现实具备足够的常识，能够不作抵抗地走向消亡，就会和平地完成替代；若它抗拒这种必然性，则将以暴力方式取而代之。因此，黑格尔的命题通过黑格尔辩证法本身转化为其对立面：人类历史领域中一切现实的事物，随着时间的推移都会变得不合理，因此按其自身的规定就注定变得不合理，从一开始就背负着不合理；而人们心中一切合理的事物，无论它与现存的表象现实多么矛盾，都注定会成为现实。按照黑格尔思维方法的所有规则，“一切现实皆具理性”这一命题被消解，从而转化为另一命题：一切存在之物都理应消亡。
en: Now, according to Hegel, reality is, however, in no way an attribute predicable of any given state of affairs, social or political, in all circumstances and at all times. On the contrary. The Roman Republic was real, but so was the Roman Empire, which superseded it.
