In 1789 the French monarchy had become so unreal, that is to say, so robbed of all necessity, so irrational, that it had to be destroyed by the Great Revolution, of which Hegel always speaks with the greatest enthusiasm. In this case, therefore, the monarchy was the unreal and the revolution the real. And so, in the course of development, all that was previously real becomes unreal, loses its necessity, its right of existence, its rationality. And in the place of moribund reality comes a new, viable reality – peacefully if the old has enough common sense to go to its death without a struggle; forcibly if it resists this necessity. Thus the Hegelian proposition turns into its opposite through Hegelian dialectics itself: All that is real in the sphere of human history becomes irrational in the course of time, is therefore irrational by its very destination, is encumbered with irrationality from the outset; and everything which is rational in the minds of men is destined to become real, however much it may contradict existing apparent reality. In accordance with all the rules of the Hegelian method of thought, the proposition of the rationality of everything which is real is dissolved to become the other proposition: All that exists deserves to perish.

zh: 一种既定的社会形式，其“合理性”程度取决于它能否实现其目的，即能否发展生产力、提高文化水平，从而推动人类进步。一旦它无法做到这一点，就会与自身产生矛盾——也就是说，它便变得不合理且不现实，不再具有任何存在的权利。因此，即使在黑格尔那些看似最反动的言论中，也隐藏着革命的思想。
en: A given form of society is ‘rational’ to the degree that it achieves its purpose, that is, that it develops the productive forces, raises the cultural level, and thus advances human progress. Once it fails to do this, it enters into contradiction with itself – that is, it becomes irrational and unreal, and no longer has any right to exist. Thus, even in the most apparently reactionary utterances of Hegel, there is hidden a revolutionary idea.

zh: 显然，一切存在都是出于必然性。但并非一切都能存在。潜在的存在还不是现实的存在。在《逻辑学》中，黑格尔仔细追溯了事物从仅仅可能的状态，到可能性变成概率，进而概率变成必然性（“必然性”）的过程。鉴于现代科学在“概率”问题上产生的巨大混乱，研究黑格尔对这一主题的透彻而深刻的论述具有极高的启发性。
en: All that exists evidently does so out of necessity. But not everything can exist. Potential existence is not yet actual existence. In The Science of Logic, Hegel carefully traces the process whereby something passes from a state of being merely possible to the point where possibility becomes probability, and the latter becomes inevitable (‘necessity’). In view of the colossal confusion that has arisen in modern science around the issue of ‘probability’, a study of Hegel’s thorough and profound treatment of this subject is highly instructive.

zh: 可能性与现实性标志着现实世界的辩证发展以及事物的产生与发展所经历的各个阶段。一种以潜在形式存在的事物，在其内部蕴含着客观的发展趋势，或者至少不存在会阻碍其产生的条件。然而，抽象可能性与现实潜在性之间存在差异，二者却常被混为一谈。抽象或形式上的可能性仅仅表明不存在任何可能排除特定现象出现的条件，但并不假定存在会使其出现成为必然的条件。
en: Possibility and actuality denote the dialectical development of the real world and the various stages in the emergence and development of objects. A thing which exists in potential contains within itself the objective tendency of development, or at least the absence of conditions which would preclude its coming into being. However, there is a difference between abstract possibility and real potential, and the two things are frequently confused. Abstract or formal possibility merely expresses the absence of any conditions that might exclude a particular phenomenon, but it does not assume the presence of conditions which would make its appearance inevitable.

zh: 这会导致无休止的混淆，实际上是一种诡辩伎俩，旨在为各种荒谬而武断的想法提供依据。例如，有人说，如果让一只猴子在打字机上敲打足够长的时间，它最终会写出一首莎士比亚的十四行诗。这个目标似乎太过保守了。为什么只是一首十四行诗？为什么不是莎士比亚的全集呢？事实上，为什么不直接涵盖整个世界文学，再顺便把广义相对论和贝多芬的交响曲也一并算进去呢？仅仅断言这是“统计上可能的”，并不能让我们向前迈进一步。自然、社会和人类思想的复杂过程并非都能用简单的统计方法来处理，而且，无论我们等待那只猴子产出杰作多久，伟大的文学作品都不会仅仅凭偶然出现。
en: This leads to endless confusion, and is actually a kind of trick which serves to justify all kinds of absurd and arbitrary ideas. For example, it is said that if a monkey were allowed to hammer away at a typewriter for long enough, it would eventually produce one of Shakespeare’s sonnets. This objective seems too modest. Why only one sonnet? Why not the collected works of Shakespeare? Indeed, why not the whole of world literature, with the general theory of relativity and Beethoven’s symphonies thrown in for good measure? The bare assertion that it is ‘statistically possible’ does not take us a single step further. The complex processes of nature, society and human thought are not all susceptible to simple statistical treatment, nor will great works of literature emerge out of mere accident, no matter how long we wait for our monkey to deliver the goods.

zh: 要使潜在的成为现实的，需要特定的条件组合。此外，这并非一个简单的线性过程，而是一个辩证的过程，其中微小的量变积累最终会产生质的飞跃。与抽象的可能性相对，现实的可能性意味着所有必要因素都已具备，在此基础上，潜在的才会摆脱其暂时的性质，从而成为现实的。而且，正如黑格尔所阐释的，它只会在这类条件存在期间保持为现实，一旦条件不复存在，现实性便随之消逝。无论我们讨论的是个体的生命、某种社会经济形态、科学理论，还是任何自然现象，这一规律都成立。变化变得不可避免的临界点，可以通过黑格尔所创立的、被称为“度的节点线”的方法来确定。如果我们将任何过程视为一条线，就会发现发展轨迹上存在特定的点（“节点”），在这些点上，该过程会经历突然的加速或质的飞跃。
en: In order for potential to become actual, a particular concatenation of circumstances is required. Moreover, this is not a simple, linear process, but a dialectical one, in which an accumulation of small quantitative changes eventually produces a qualitative leap. Real, as opposed to abstract, possibility implies the presence of all the necessary factors out of which the potential will lose its character of provisionality, and become actual. And, as Hegel explains, it will remain actual only for as long as these conditions exist, and no longer. This is true whether we are referring to the life of an individual, a given socioeconomic form, a scientific theory, or any natural phenomenon. The point at which a change becomes inevitable can be determined by the method invented by Hegel and known as the ‘nodal line of measurement’. If we regard any process as a line, it will be seen that there are specific points (‘nodal points’) on the line of development, where the process experiences a sudden acceleration, or qualitative leap.

zh: 在孤立的案例中，如用球棒击打球时，识别因果关系很容易。但在更广泛的意义上，因果关系的概念则变得复杂得多。个别的原因和结果在巨大的相互作用之海中消失了，在那里，原因会转化为结果，反之亦然。试着将即使是最简单的事件追溯到其“最终原因”，你就会发现，即使永恒的时间也不足以完成这项工作。总会涌现出新的原因，而这个原因又需要进一步解释，如此循环往复，无穷无尽。这一悖论已通过如下谚语深入大众意识：
en: It is easy to identify cause and effect in isolated cases, as when one hits a ball with a bat. But in a wider sense, the notion of causality becomes far more complicated. Individual causes and effects become lost in a vast ocean of interaction, where cause becomes transformed into effect and vice versa. Just try tracing back even the simplest event to its ‘ultimate causes’ and you will see that eternity will not be long enough to do it. There will always be some new cause, and that in turn will have to be explained, and so on ad infinitum. This paradox has entered the popular consciousness in such sayings as this one:

zh: 因缺了一枚钉子，丢了一只马蹄铁；
因缺了一只马蹄铁，丢了一匹马；
因缺了一匹马，丢了一名骑手；
因缺了一名骑手，输了一场战役；
因输了一场战役，丢了一个王国；
……而这一切，皆因缺了一枚钉子。
en: For the want of a nail, a shoe was lost;
For the want of a shoe, a horse was lost;
For the want of a horse, a rider was lost;
For the want of a rider, a battle was lost;
For the want of a battle, a kingdom was lost;
…And all for the want of a nail.

zh: 由于无法确立“终极原因”，有些人干脆彻底放弃了“原因”这一概念。一切都被视为随机且偶然的。在二十世纪，许多科学家——至少在理论上——基于对量子物理学结果——尤其是维尔纳·海森堡的哲学立场——的错误解读，采纳了这一立场。我们此前已对此进行了详尽探讨。
这里只需指出，黑格尔在阐释偶然性与必然性之间的辩证关系时，早已预先回应了这些论点。
en: The impossibility of establishing a ‘final cause’ has led some people to abandon the idea of cause altogether. Everything is considered to be random and accidental. In the twentieth century this position was adopted, at least in theory, by a large number of scientists on the basis of an incorrect interpretation of the results of quantum physics, particularly the philosophical positions of Werner Heisenberg. We have dealt with this matter at length before.
Suffice it here to say that Hegel answered these arguments in advance, when he explained the dialectical relation between accident and necessity.

zh: 黑格尔阐明，就孤立的原因与结果这一意义而言，并不存在真正的因果关系。每一个结果都有其反作用，每一个作用都有其反作用。孤立的因果关系这一概念，是源自古典牛顿物理学的抽象概念，尽管当时它享有极高的声望，但黑格尔对此却提出了严厉的批评。在这方面，黑格尔再次领先于他的时代。他摒弃了力学中的“作用-反作用”原理，提出了“交互作用”的概念，即普遍的相互作用。万物相互影响，同时又被万物所影响和决定。因此，黑格尔重新引入了“偶然性”这一概念——该概念曾被牛顿和拉普拉斯的机械论哲学严格排除在科学之外。
en: Hegel explains that there is no such thing as true causality, in the sense of an isolated cause and effect. Every effect has a counter-effect, and every action has a counter-action. The idea of an isolated cause and effect is an abstraction taken from classical Newtonian physics, which Hegel was highly critical of, although it enjoyed tremendous prestige at that time. Here again, Hegel was in advance of his time. Instead of the action-reaction of mechanics, he advanced the notion of Reciprocity, of universal interaction. Everything influences everything else and is, in turn, influenced and determined by everything. Hegel thus re-introduced the concept of accident which had been rigorously banned from science by the mechanist philosophy of Newton and Laplace.

zh: 乍看之下，我们似乎迷失在无数偶然之中。但这种混乱只是表象。秩序从混沌中显现。那些如同海面波涛般不断闪现又消逝的偶然现象，表达着一个更深层的进程——这个进程并非偶然，而是必然的。在决定性的时刻，这种必然性通过偶然性显现出来。
en: At first sight, we seem to be lost in a vast number of accidents. But this confusion is only apparent. Order emerges out of chaos. The accidental phenomena which constantly flash in and out of existence, like the waves on the surface of an ocean, express a deeper process, which is not accidental but necessary. At a decisive point, this necessity reveals itself through accident.

zh: 这种关于必然性与偶然性辩证统一的观点或许显得陌生，但来自科学和社会各领域的一系列观察结果却有力地证实了这一点。进化论中的自然选择机制便是最广为人知的例子，但还有许多其他例子。在过去的半个世纪里，混沌理论和复杂性理论领域取得了许多发现，这些发现恰恰详细阐述了“秩序如何从混沌中产生”，这正是黑格尔一个半世纪前所阐明的。
en: This idea of the dialectical unity of necessity and accident may seem strange, but it is strikingly confirmed by a whole series of observations from the most varied fields of science and society. The mechanism of natural selection in the theory of evolution is the best-known example. But there are many others. In the last half century, there have been many discoveries in the field of chaos and complexity theory which precisely detail how ‘order arises out of chaos’, which is exactly what Hegel worked out one and a half centuries earlier.

zh: “经典”化学反应被视为高度随机的过程。参与反应的分子在空间中均匀分布，其分布呈“正态”分布，即高斯曲线。此类反应符合玻尔兹曼的理论，即反应的所有支路最终都会消失，反应将趋于一种稳定的反应状态——即静止平衡。然而，在近几十年间，人们发现了一些偏离这一理想且简化的概念的化学反应。最著名的例子是贝洛索夫-扎博廷斯基反应，以及混沌理论学家伊利亚·普里戈金提出的布鲁塞尔模型。
en: ‘Classical’ chemical reactions are seen as very random processes. The molecules involved are evenly distributed in space, and their spread is distributed ‘normally’ i.e. in a Gauss curve. These kinds of reactions fit into the concept of Boltzmann, wherein all side-chains of the reaction will fade out and the reaction will end up in a stable reaction, an immobile equilibrium. However, in recent decades chemical reactions were discovered that deviate from this ideal and simplified concept. The most famous examples are the Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction, and the Brussels model devised by chaos theorist Ilya Prigogine.

zh: 线性热力学描述了系统趋向于最低可能活动水平的稳定、可预测行为。然而，当作用于系统的热力学力达到超越线性区域的临界点时，便无法再假设系统处于稳定状态。此时，湍流便产生了。长期以来，湍流一直被视为无序或混沌的同义词。但如今人们发现，那些在宏观（大尺度）层面看似纯粹的混沌无序，实际上在微观（小尺度）层面却具有高度的组织性。
en: Linear thermodynamics describes a stable, predictable behaviour of systems that tend towards the minimum level of activity possible. However, when the thermodynamic forces acting on a system reach the point where the linear region is exceeded, stability can no longer be assumed. Turbulence arises. For a long time, turbulence was regarded as a synonym for disorder or chaos. But now, it has been discovered that, what appears to be merely chaotic disorder on the macroscopic (large-scale) level, is, in fact, highly organised on the microscopic (small-scale) level.

zh: 如今，对化学不稳定性的研究已十分普遍。其中，在布鲁塞尔由伊利亚·普里戈金指导进行的关于“化学时钟”现象的研究尤为引人关注。从辩证法的角度来看，对化学不稳定性开始的临界点之后所发生现象的研究具有巨大的研究价值。布鲁塞尔模型（被美国科学家昵称为“布鲁塞拉托”）描述了气体分子的行为。假设存在两种分子——“红色”和“蓝色”——它们处于混沌的、完全随机的运动状态。人们会预期，在某个特定时刻，分子的分布会不均匀，从而呈现“紫色”，偶尔闪现红色或蓝色。但在化学钟中，超过临界点后情况并非如此。系统会先全部呈蓝色，随后全部呈红色，且这些变化以固定间隔发生。
en: Today, the study of chemical instabilities has become common. Of special interest is the research done on the phenomenon of the ‘chemical clock’ in Brussels under the guidance of Ilya Prigogine. The study of what happens beyond the critical point where chemical instability commences has enormous interest from the standpoint of dialectics. The Brussels model (nicknamed the ‘Brusselator’ by American scientists) describes the behaviour of gas molecules. Suppose there are two types of molecules, ‘red’ and ‘blue’, in a state of chaotic, totally random motion. One would expect that, at a given moment, there would be an irregular distribution of molecules, producing a ‘violet’ colour, with occasional flashes of red or blue. But in a chemical clock, this does not occur beyond the critical point. The system is all blue, then all red, and these changes occur at regular intervals.

zh: 源自数十亿分子活动所产生的这种秩序程度似乎难以置信，事实上，如果未曾观测到化学钟，没有人会相信这样的过程是可能的。要瞬间改变颜色，分子必须有一种“沟通”的方式。该系统必须作为一个整体来行动。我们将反复提及这个关键词——“沟通”，它在从化学到神经生理学的众多领域中显然具有重要意义。耗散结构可能为这样的沟通提供了一种最简单的物理机制。
en: Such a degree of order stemming from the activity of billions of molecules seems incredible and indeed, if chemical clocks had not been observed, no one would believe that such a process is possible. To change colour all at once, molecules must have a way to “communicate”. The system has to act as a whole. We will return repeatedly to this key word, communicate, which is of obvious importance in so many fields, from chemistry to neurophysiology. Dissipative structures introduce probably one of the simplest physical mechanisms for communication.

zh: “化学时钟”现象展示了自然界中秩序如何在某个节点自发地从混沌中产生。这是一个重要的观察结果，特别是在生命如何从无机物中产生这一问题上。
en: The phenomenon of the ‘chemical clock’ shows how in nature order can arise spontaneously out of chaos at a certain point. This is an important observation, especially in relation to the way in which life arises from inorganic matter.

zh: “通过涨落产生秩序”的模型描绘了一个不稳定的世界，其中微小的原因可能产生巨大的影响，但这个世界并非任意而为。恰恰相反，微小事件得以放大的原因，是理性探究的正当对象。
en: “Order through fluctuations” models introduce an unstable world where small causes can have large effects, but this world is not arbitrary. On the contrary, the reasons for the amplification of a small event are a legitimate matter for rational inquiry.

zh: 我们必须记住，黑格尔写作于上个世纪初，当时科学完全受古典力学物理学的支配，而且比达尔文通过随机突变提出自然选择理论还要早半个世纪。他没有任何科学证据来支持其理论——即必然性通过偶然性来表现这一理论。但这正是科学领域最新创新思维背后的核心思想。
en: We must remember that Hegel was writing at the beginning of the last century, when science was completely dominated by classical mechanical physics, and half a century before Darwin developed the idea of natural selection through the medium of random mutations. He had no scientific evidence to back up his theory that necessity expresses itself through accident. But that is the central idea behind the most recent innovative thinking in science.

zh: 这一深刻规律对于理解历史同样至关重要。正如马克思1871 年在致库格尔曼的信中写道：
en: This profound law is equally fundamental to an understanding of history. As Marx wrote to Kugelmann in 1871:

zh: 如果斗争仅在绝对有利的条件下进行，那么世界历史确实会非常容易创造。反之，如果“偶然”不发挥任何作用，世界历史又将具有非常神秘的性质。这些偶然本身自然地融入了总体的发展进程，并又被其他偶然所抵消。但进程的加速与延迟在很大程度上取决于此类“偶然”，其中包括那些最初站在运动最前沿的人的性格这一“偶然”。
en: World history would indeed be very easy to make, if the struggle were taken up only on condition of infallibly favourable chances. It would on the other hand be of a very mystical nature, if “accidents” played no part. These accidents themselves fall naturally into the general course of development and are compensated for, again, by other accidents. But acceleration and delay are very dependent upon such “acci dents” which include the “accident” of the character of those who at first stand at the head of the movement.

zh: 恩格斯在几年后谈及“伟人”在历史中的作用时，也表达了同样的观点：
en: Engels made the same point a few years later in relation to the role of ‘great men’ in history:

zh: 人自己创造历史，但还不是凭借集体意志，也非按照集体计划，甚至不是在明确界定的、既定的社会中进行。他们的努力相互冲突，正因如此，所有这样的社会都受制于必然性，而这种必然性又通过偶然性得到补充，并以偶然性的形式呈现出来。在此所有偶然性之中彰显出来的必然性，归根结底仍是经济必然性。这就是所谓“伟人”需要加以探讨的地方。某个人——而且恰恰是那个人——在特定时间、特定国家出现，当然纯属偶然。但如果将他剔除，就会产生对替代者的需求，而这个替代者终将被找到，无论好坏，但从长远来看，他终将被找到。
en: Men make their history themselves, but not as yet with a collective will or according to a collective plan or even in a definitely defined, given society. Their efforts clash, and for that very reason all such societies are governed by necessity, which is supplemented by and appears under the forms of accident. The necessity which here asserts itself amidst all accident is again ultimately economic necessity. This is where the so-called great men come in for treatment. That such and such a man and precisely that man arises at that particular time in that given country is of course pure accident. But cut him out and there will be a demand for a substitute, and this sub stitute will be found, good or bad, but in the long run he will be found.

zh: “概念”
en: THE NOTION

zh: 在黑格尔的辩证法中，思维的最高成就便是“概念”。黑格尔将“概念”的发展描述为一个从抽象到具体的进程。它意味着知识的深化，以及理解从较低层次向较高层次的发展，即从潜在到现实的发展。起初，“概念”被称为“自在的”，或隐含的。随后，它得到发展，成为“自为”的概念，即显性概念。在其最高形式中，它是这两个方面的统一，即“自在自为”。在概念中，发展过程达到了顶点。起初仅为隐含的内容，如今变得显性。这是一种回归起点，但处于质上更高的层面。
en: In Hegel’s dialectic the supreme achievement of thought is the Notion. The development of the Notion is described by Hegel as a process which proceeds from abstract to concrete. It signifies a deepening of knowledge, and a development from a lower to a higher degree of understanding, of the development from potential to actual. At the beginning, the Notion is referred to as ‘in itself’, or implicit. It is later developed, and becomes the Notion ‘for itself’, or explicit. In its highest form it is the union of both these aspects, ‘in and for itself’. In the Notion the process of development reaches its highest point. What was only implicit at the beginning now becomes explicit. It is a return to the starting point, but on a qualitatively higher level.

zh: 在黑格尔的主要著作《逻辑学》中，他并未止步于“概念”，而是继续探讨“绝对理念”——关于这一点，唯一能说的是，他对此完全未作任何阐述。这正是黑格尔唯心主义所陷入的矛盾的典型体现。辩证法无法导向“绝对理念”，也无法导向任何其他最终的解决方案。暗示人类认识过程存在终点，这与辩证法的字面意义和精神相悖。因此，黑格尔哲学最终陷入了无法化解的矛盾。要解决这一矛盾，唯有彻底决裂于此前的一切哲学。
en: In his main work, The Science of Logic, Hegel does not end with the Notion, but goes on to the Absolute Idea, of which all that can be said is that he tells us absolutely nothing about it. This is typical of the contradictions Hegel’s idealism landed him in. The dialectic cannot lead to an Absolute Idea, or any other final solution. To imply that there is an end to the process of human knowledge conflicts with the letter and spirit of dialectics. So the Hegelian philosophy ended up in an insoluble contradiction. This could only be solved by a radical break with all of previous philosophy.

zh: 黑格尔哲学的划时代意义在于：他以如此全面的方式总结了整个哲学史，使得沿袭传统哲学路线再难向前推进。其次，他所完善的辩证法，为一种全新的世界观奠定了基础——这种世界观不局限于对思想的分析和批判，还涉及对社会历史的分析，以及对现有社会秩序的革命性批判。恩格斯在《反杜林论》中很好地阐明了黑格尔的伟大贡献：
en: The epoch-making quality of Hegel’s philosophy consisted in the fact that, by summing up the whole history of philosophy in such a comprehensive way, he made it impossible to proceed any further along the traditional philosophical lines. Secondly, the dialectical method, which he perfected, provided the basis for a whole new world outlook, one that did not confine itself to the analysis and criticism of ideas, but involved an analysis of the history of society and a revolutionary criticism of the existing social order. Hegel’s great contribution was well expressed by Engels in Anti-Dühring:

zh: 黑格尔体系没有解决它所提出的那个问题，这一点在这里并不重要。它的划时代功绩在于提出了这个问题。这个问题是任何单个人都永远无法解决的。尽管黑格尔——与圣西门一样——是当时最具百科全书式学识的思想家，但他仍受到两方面的限制：第一，他自身知识的范围必然有限；第二，他所处时代知识和观念的广度与深度也有限。除此之外，还必须加上第三个局限。黑格尔是一位唯心主义者。对他而言，脑海中的思想并非对实际事物和过程或多或少抽象的再现，相反，事物及其演变仅仅是“理念”的实现，这种“理念”早在世界存在之前就已永恒地存在于某处。这种思维方式将一切颠倒过来，彻底扭转了世界上事物的实际联系。尽管黑格尔对许多个别事实群的把握既准确又精妙，但基于上述原因，其中仍有许多地方处理得笨拙、生硬、牵强——简而言之，在细节上存在谬误。黑格尔体系本身就是一场巨大的失败——但它也是同类体系中的最后一个。事实上，它正遭受着一种内在的、无法治愈的矛盾。一方面，其基本命题是认为人类历史是一个演化过程，而这种过程就其本质而言，不可能在发现任何所谓的“绝对真理”中找到其智识上的终点。但另一方面，它却声称自己正是这一绝对真理的本质。一个包罗万象且永恒终极的自然与历史知识体系，这与辩证推理的基本法则相矛盾。事实上，这一法则绝非排斥——恰恰相反，它包含着这样一种观念：对外部宇宙的系统性认识可以在各个时代之间取得巨大飞跃。
en: That [the] Hegel[ian system] did not solve the problem [it propounded] is here immaterial. Its epoch-making merit was that it propounded the problem. This problem is one that no single individual will ever be able to solve. Although Hegel was – with Saint-Simon – the most encyclopaedic mind of his time, he was limited, first, by the necessarily limited extent of his own knowledge and, second, by the limited extent and depth of the knowledge and conceptions of his age. To these limits a third must be added. Hegel was an idealist. To him the thoughts within his brain were not the more or less abstract pictures of actual things and processes, but, conversely, things and their evolution were only the realised pictures of the ‘Idea’, existing somewhere from eternity before the world existed. This way of thinking turned everything upside down, and completely reversed the actual connection of things in the world. Correctly and ingeniously as many individual groups of facts were grasped by Hegel, yet, for the reasons just given, there is much that is botched, artificial, laboured, in a word, wrong in point of detail. The Hegelian system, in itself, was a colossal miscarriage – but it was also the last of its kind. It was suffering, in fact, from an internal and incurable contradiction. Upon the one hand, its essential proposition was the conception that human history is a process of evolution, which, by its very nature, cannot find its intellectual final term in the discovery of any so-called absolute truth. But, on the other hand, it laid claim to being the very essence of this absolute truth. A system of natural and historical knowledge, embracing everything, and final for all time, is a contradiction to the fundamental law of dialectic reasoning. This law, indeed, by no means excludes, but, on the contrary, includes the idea that systematic knowledge of the external universe can make giant strides from age to age.

zh: 黑格尔的辩证法构思精妙，但终究存在缺陷，因为它仅局限于思想领域。尽管如此，它蕴含着思想领域重大突破的潜力，这种突破不仅将彻底改变哲学史，还将彻底改变世界史。借用黑格尔的话来说，在他著作中“自在”（即潜在）的观念，在马克思主义这一革命性学说中成为了一个实现的观念——一个“自在自为的”观念；在此，哲学终于摆脱了作为片面抽象的思维活动的性质，进入了实践的领域。
en: Hegel’s dialectic was brilliantly conceived, but ultimately deficient, because it was limited to the domain of thought. Nevertheless, it contained the potential for a major departure in thought, one that was to radically alter not just the history of philosophy, but that of the world. To paraphrase Hegel, what was present in itself (i.e. potentially) in his work became a realised idea – an idea in and for itself in the revolutionary doctrine of Marxism, where philosophy finally gives up its character as a one-sided abstract, mental activity, and enters the realm of practice.

zh: 亚里士多德早已阐明了“潜能”与“现实”之间的关系。在自然、社会、思想的各个层面，甚至在个体从童年到成熟的发展过程中，我们都能看到同样的过程。一切存在之物都蕴含着进一步发展的潜能，即完善自身、蜕变为与当下不同的存在。整个人类历史可以被视为人类为实现自身潜能而进行的斗争。归根结底，社会主义的目标是创造必要的条件，使这一目标最终得以实现，让男女都能真正成为他们潜在的模样。然而，此时我们已经离开了哲学家那间光线昏暗的书房，步入了人类生活、活动与斗争的灿烂阳光之下。
en: Aristotle already explained the relationship between potential and actual. At all levels of nature, society, thought, and even the development of individual human beings from childhood to maturity, we see the same process. Everything that exists contains within itself the potential for further development, that is, to perfect itself, to become something different to what it is. The whole of human history can be seen as the struggle of humanity to realise its potential. Ultimately, the aim of socialism is to create the necessary conditions whereby this goal can be finally realised, that men and women can become actually what they always were potentially. Here, however, we have already left the dimly-lit study of the philosopher, and stepped out into the broad daylight of human life, activity and struggle.
